Was ich gefunden habe, bestimmt den Entwurf:

- **Rowboats Brain-Ansicht** (`graph-view.tsx`, 678 Zeilen) ist ein selbstgeschriebener 2D-Kräftegraph in SVG. Die Notizen werden nur nach ihrem Ordner gruppiert und eingefärbt. **three.js ist im Rowboat-Frontend nicht installiert**, das müsste als neue Abhängigkeit in den Fork.
- **Die Ordner im Vault sind flach**, also `Components/*.md`, `Models/*.md`. Die Hierarchie ergibt sich erst aus den Verweisen:
  - Ein Model verweist auf `[[Brands/BMW]]`.
  - Ein Component verweist auf `[[Models/…]]` und hat `Area: Exterior / Exterior details`.
  - Ein Bauteil kann aber zu mehreren Modellen gehören, etwa die Badges zu F70, G60 und G70. Streng genommen ist das kein Baum, sondern ein Netz.

**Nächste Frage: Woraus soll die Hierarchie entstehen?** Davon hängt ab, ob die Ansicht für jeden Rowboat-Vault taugt oder nur für unseren.
- **A) Ebenen nach Notiztyp, Eltern über Verweise** (Empfehlung):
  - Eine feste Reihenfolge ordnet die Typen in Ebenen, hier etwa Brands → Models → Components → Feature Classes.
  - Jede Notiz hängt unter der Notiz der nächsthöheren Ebene, auf die sie verweist. Bei mehreren Treffern nimmt sie die erste.
  - Requirements, Purchase Drivers, Topics usw. schweben als eigene Ebene darüber und sind mit Linien verbunden.
  - Die Typ-Reihenfolge kommt aus `config/notes.json`. Damit funktioniert die Ansicht auch für andere Vaults.
- **B) Feld `parent:` im Frontmatter:** Jede Notiz nennt ihre Elternnotiz ausdrücklich. Das ist am präzisesten, aber unsere Skripte müssten das Feld in rund 160 Notizen schreiben, und fremde Vaults hätten es nicht.
- **C) Automatisch aus der Verweisstruktur:** Der am stärksten vernetzte Knoten wird zur Wurzel, und von dort entsteht ein Baum. Das braucht keine Konfiguration, ergibt aber oft keine sinnvolle Hierarchie.

Nebenbei: Der Startprozess der Demo hat sich mit Exit-Code 4 beendet. Rowboat läuft also vermutlich gerade nicht. Das prüfe ich, bevor wir testen.

## Drei Wege, aus Verweisen eine Hierarchie zu bauen

**1) Hub-Baum** (meine Empfehlung):
- Jede Notiz bekommt als Eltern ihren **am stärksten vernetzten Nachbarn**, sofern der stärker vernetzt ist als sie selbst. Notizen ohne so einen Nachbarn sind Wurzeln.
- Bei uns ergibt das genau die gewünschte Ordnung:
  - **BMW** (verweist auf alles) wird Wurzel.
  - Die **Modelle** hängen darunter.
  - Die **Bauteile** hängen unter dem Modell, mit dem sie am stärksten verbunden sind, die **Feature Classes** unter ihrem Bauteil.
  - **Requirements** hängen unter Topics oder Bauteilen.
- Vorteile: einfach, stabil, schnell bei Tausenden Notizen, für jeden Vault sinnvoll.
- Nachteil: Bei gleich starker Vernetzung entscheidet ein fester Tie-Break, etwa alphabetisch.

**2) Rekursive Community-Erkennung (Louvain):**
- Der Graph wird in Cluster zerlegt, jeder Cluster wieder in Unter-Cluster, und so weiter.
- Ergibt sehr „natürliche“ Themengruppen.
- Nachteil: Die Cluster haben keine Namen und keinen Kopf, und das Ergebnis springt bei jeder neuen Notiz. Dafür bräuchte es auch eine zusätzliche Bibliothek.

**3) Kürzeste Wege ab Wurzel:**
- Der am stärksten vernetzte Knoten wird Wurzel, die Ebenen ergeben sich aus dem Abstand in Schritten.
- Einfach, aber flach: Bauteile und Topics landen oft auf derselben Ebene, obwohl sie nichts miteinander zu tun haben.

**Darstellung, gleich für alle drei:**
- Jeder Teilbaum ist ein **Würfel im Raum**, die Kinder füllen die Achtel seines Würfels, so wie im Octree.
- Querverweise, die nicht zum Baum gehören, sind dünne Linien.
- Ein Klick auf einen Würfel zoomt hinein, ein Klick auf eine Notiz öffnet sie wie bisher.

**Passt der Hub-Baum (1)?**

Da hast du recht. Eine erratene Hierarchie ist für ein PM-Tool zu wackelig: Sie verschiebt sich bei jeder neuen Notiz, und die KI kann sich nicht darauf verlassen. Ich fasse zusammen, wie ich dich verstehe:

## Mein Verständnis
- **Ziel:** eine **einheitliche, ausdrücklich festgelegte Hierarchie**, die drei Seiten gemeinsam nutzen:
  1. der 3D-Graph zum Anordnen,
  2. die KI zum Lesen, Einordnen und Anlegen neuer Notizen,
  3. Menschen zum Pflegen.
- **Erweiterbar:** Ein neuer Notiztyp, etwa „Kampagne“ oder „Sponsor“, lässt sich an einer Stelle einhängen, ohne Code zu ändern.
- **Wartbar:** Die Struktur steht an einer Stelle, und ob sie eingehalten wird, lässt sich prüfen.
- **Meine Annahme:** Es ist im Grunde A, aber **allgemein statt BMW-spezifisch**. Ich vermute, A war für dich deshalb nicht übertragbar.

## Vorschlag: feste Ebenen plus ein ausdrückliches `parent:`

**1. Fünf allgemeine Ebenen**, wie in PM-Tools üblich (Portfolio, Projekt, Epic, Story, Task):

| Ebene | Bedeutung | Bei uns | Bei EHL-PM |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Organisation | wem es gehört | Brands/BMW | EHL |
| L1 Vorhaben | Produkt, Projekt, Programm | Models/G60 | Event 2026 |
| L2 Bereich | Teilgebiet, Workstream | Area (Exterior/Cockpit) | Sponsoring, Marketing |
| L3 Einheit | das, worüber man entscheidet | Components, Requirements | Sponsor, Kampagne, Task |
| L4 Detail | Belege, Unterpunkte | Feature Classes, Zitate | Mail, Notiz, Subtask |

**2. Jeder Notiztyp bekommt in `config/notes.json` eine Ebene.** Dort definiert Rowboat die Typen schon heute, wir fügen nur `level` und `parentTypes` hinzu. Ein neuer Typ heißt also: eine Zeile in der Konfiguration.

**3. Jede Notiz nennt ihre Eltern ausdrücklich** im Frontmatter mit `parent: "[[Models/5er G60]]"`. Genau ein Elternteil. Damit ist es ein echter Baum, eben ein Octree. Alle anderen `[[Links]]` bleiben Querverbindungen.

**4. Pflege:**
- **Rowboats Notiz-Agenten** setzen `parent` beim Anlegen, weil es in der Vorlage jedes Typs steht.
- **Ein Prüfskript** meldet Notizen ohne gültiges `parent` und schlägt per Hub-Regel eines vor. Das erledigt auch die einmalige Migration unserer rund 190 Notizen.

**5. Der 3D-Graph** liest nur `level` und `parent`. Jede Ebene ist eine Schale, jeder Teilbaum ein Würfel, die Querverweise sind Linien.

**Passen die fünf Ebenen so, oder fehlt dir eine?** Mögliche Lücken wären eine Ebene für Zeit, also Meilenstein oder Sprint, oder für Personen.
und für sämtliche buisness daten?

Gute Frage, und sie ändert das Bild. **Geschäftsdaten passen nicht in einen einzigen Baum.** Ein Sponsor-Kontakt gehört zu einer Firma, zu einem Projekt, zu einer Kampagne, hat Mails und einen Termin. Würde man ihn nur an einer Stelle einhängen, wäre er von den anderen Seiten aus „unsichtbar“. Deshalb schlage ich zwei Teile vor:

## 1. Ein Hauptbaum: wo eine Notiz „wohnt“

Ganz oben stehen **sechs feste Domänen** für alle Geschäftsdaten. Darunter gelten die bekannten Ebenen. Jede Notiz hat genau **ein** `parent:`, und das ist die Ordnung für den 3D-Graphen.

| L1 Domäne | L2 / L3 / L4, Beispiele | Quelle |
|---|---|---|
| **Organisation** | Team → Person → Rolle | Team, Rowboat |
| **Markt & Kunden** | Segment → Firma → Kontakt | **Sales-Claw** |
| **Angebot** | Produkt → Komponente/Requirement → Feature Class | Dataset, Torque |
| **Vorhaben** | Projekt/Event → Workstream → Task, Kampagne | PM, **Marketing** |
| **Kommunikation** | Kanal → Mail/Meeting/Post/Newsletter | Gmail, Meetings, **Marketing** |
| **Wissen & Belege** | Quelle → Studie/Datensatz → Fund/Zitat | Dataset, Research, RAG |

Darüber liegt L0, die eigene Organisation, zum Beispiel EHL.

## 2. Querbezüge mit Typ: wie eine Notiz mit dem Rest zusammenhängt

Statt nackter `[[Links]]` gibt es **einen kleinen festen Satz benannter Beziehungen** im Frontmatter:

- `customer:` → Firma oder Kontakt
- `project:` → Vorhaben
- `owner:` → Person
- `about:` → Produkt oder Komponente
- `evidence:` → Beleg
- `when:` → Datum oder Meilenstein

Beispiel: Eine Mail an einen Sponsor wohnt unter *Kommunikation → E-Mail* und trägt `customer: [[Firma X]]`, `project: [[EHL 2026]]`, `owner: [[Felix]]`.

**Was das bringt:**
- **3D-Graph:** Der Hauptbaum bildet die Würfel. Die Beziehungen sind Linien, die sich nach Typ ein- und ausblenden lassen, zum Beispiel „zeig alles zu Firma X“.
- **KI:** Sie fragt gezielt („alle Mails mit `customer` = X“), statt im Text zu raten. Beim Anlegen sagt ihr die Vorlage, welche Felder Pflicht sind.
- **Erweiterbar:** Ein neuer Typ bekommt in `notes.json` eine Domäne, eine Ebene und seine erlaubten Beziehungen. Eine neue Beziehung ist ebenfalls nur eine Zeile dort.
- **Wartbar:** Ein Prüfskript meldet fehlende `parent`-Angaben, Pflichtbeziehungen und kaputte Ziele.

**Passen die sechs Domänen und die sechs Beziehungen**, oder fehlt dir ein Geschäftsbereich, etwa **Finanzen** mit Budget, Rechnungen und Sponsoring-Beträgen?
okay

Gut, dann gelten die **sechs Domänen, die Ebenen L0–L4, genau ein `parent` pro Notiz und sechs benannte Beziehungen**. Finanzen lasse ich vorerst weg; die Domäne lässt sich später als Zeile in der Konfiguration ergänzen.

**Das ist zu groß für eine einzige Spec.** Ich schlage vor, es in vier Teilprojekte zu zerlegen. Jedes bekommt eine eigene Spec, einen eigenen Plan und eine eigene Umsetzung:

| # | Teilprojekt | Wo | Hängt ab von |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Schema**: Domänen, Ebenen und Beziehungen in `notes.json`, dazu ein Prüf- und Migrationsskript, das allen ~190 Notizen `parent` und Beziehungen gibt | unser Repo (`schema/`), Vault | – |
| **2** | **3D-Ansicht**: Rowboats Brain liest `parent` und `level`, zeigt die Hierarchie als verschachtelte Würfel (Octree) und die Beziehungen als filterbare Linien | Fork `Flissel/rowboat`, `graph-view.tsx`, three.js neu | 1 |
| **3** | **KI pflegt mit**: Die Vorlagen der Notiztypen verlangen `parent` und Pflichtbeziehungen, Rowboats Notiz-Agenten setzen sie beim Anlegen | `notes.json`-Vorlagen und Prompts | 1 |
| **4** | **Geschäftsdaten einhängen**: Sales-Claw (Firmen, Kontakte) und Marketing (Kampagnen, Posts) schreiben Notizen mit `parent` und Beziehungen in den Vault (WP2-Brücke) | `bridge/` | 1 |

**Reihenfolge:** Zuerst **1**, weil alles andere daran hängt. Danach **2**, weil das der sichtbare Effekt ist. 3 und 4 können parallel laufen.

**Ein Punkt zu 2:** Dafür muss Rowboat selbst geändert werden. In `why-rowboat.md` steht derzeit „unverändert auf `72e9d8c`“. Nach dem Merge passe ich den Text an, auf etwa „ein kleiner, klar benannter Patch für die 3D-Ansicht im Fork“.

# Vault filesystem for an AI company – iteration 1 (draft)

Goal: one uniform, extensible hierarchy for ALL business data of an AI company, used by Rowboat's
3D brain graph, by AI agents (read, classify, write) and by humans. Each note has exactly one
`parent` (primary tree) plus typed relations. Rowboat facts: built-in note types People,
Organizations, Projects, Topics, Meetings with fixed top-level folders, written by Rowboat's own
agents from mail/meetings; graph groups by first path segment, uses depth; note types are
configured in config/notes.json (type, folder, template, extractionGuide).

## Levels
L0 Company (one root note) · L1 Domain · L2 Area · L3 Entity (what you decide/act on) · L4 Detail/evidence

## Domains (L1) and areas (L2) – AI company capability map
1. Strategy & Governance – vision/OKRs, board & investors, legal entity, policies, risks, AI ethics/compliance (EU AI Act, GDPR)
2. Organisation & People – team, roles, hiring, onboarding, freelancers, AI agents as workers
3. Product & Technology – products, features/requirements, roadmap, architecture, repos, releases, incidents
4. AI & Data – models, prompts, agents, evaluations, datasets, training/fine-tuning runs, compute/GPU, vendors (LLM APIs)
5. Market & Customers – segments, organizations, contacts, leads/pipeline (Sales-Claw), partners, competitors
6. Marketing & Communication – brand, campaigns, content, channels, newsletters, social posts, events
7. Delivery & Projects – customer projects, internal initiatives, milestones, tasks, sprints
8. Finance – budget, revenue, invoices, costs (incl. compute/API spend), funding, grants, pricing
9. Operations & Infrastructure – tools/SaaS, servers (Proxmox, mini PC), security, secrets policy, vendors/contracts
10. Knowledge & Evidence – sources, studies, datasets as documents, research findings, quotes
11. Communication records – mails, meetings, chats, voice memos (raw inputs)

## Filesystem
Option F1 (Rowboat-compatible): top-level folder = note TYPE (flat, as Rowboat expects); domain,
level, parent live in front matter.
Option F2 (browsable): Domain/Type/Note.md, e.g. `05 Market/Organizations/Acme.md`; Rowboat's
built-in folders remapped in notes.json.
Draft picks F2 for browsability.

## Front matter (every note)
type, domain, level, parent: "[[...]]", relations: customer, project, owner, about, evidence, when;
status; updated; source; managed_by.

## Relations
customer, project, owner, about, evidence, when

# Vault schema: one hierarchy for all business data of an AI company

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** draft for review (sub-project 1 of 4) · **Iterations:** 3
(draft → business critique + Rowboat/AI critique → this version)

## 1. Goal

One uniform, extensible and maintainable hierarchy for **all** business data of an AI company. It is
read by three consumers:

- **Rowboat's 3D brain graph** (sub-project 2) arranges notes as nested cells (octree) along this
  hierarchy.
- **AI agents** read, classify and write notes along it, without guessing from free text.
- **People** keep it up to date.

**Success criteria**

- Every note has exactly one `parent`, and the parents form one tree per vault (no cycles).
- A new note type or relation is a few lines in one schema file. Nobody touches code for it.
- A linter in CI proves that every note follows the schema.
- Rowboat keeps working unmodified with the vault: its own agents still write `People/`, `Organizations/`
  and the other built-in folders, links still resolve, and duplicate detection still works.

## 2. Findings that shaped this version

From reading Rowboat at `72e9d8c`:

| Finding | Where | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A note type's `folder` is not passed to the note agent. Prompts hard-code `knowledge/People/…`, `[[People/X]]`, `Meetings/…` | `core/src/knowledge/note_system.ts:242`, `note_creation.ts:145-179, 569-575, 1253` | **Folders stay flat, one folder per type (F1).** Domain folders (F2) would split data between old and new paths |
| People and Organizations are recognised by their **first** path segment. Dedup uses the body fields `**Aliases:**`, `**Email:**`, `**Domain:**` | `knowledge_index.ts:75-99, 254-266` | Built-in folders stay at the top level. Bridges write these body fields too |
| `[[Folder/Name]]` resolves by exact, case-sensitive path only. Renaming a folder does not rewrite links | `lib/wiki-links.ts:40-45`, `workspace/wiki-link-rewrite.ts:130` | Paths are IDs: never rename a folder, rename notes only through `aliases` |
| The properties editor drops nested YAML maps | `renderer/src/lib/frontmatter.ts:150-210` | **Front matter must be flat**: one top-level key per relation, links quoted |
| The graph groups by first path segment and skips `meetings/` | `App.tsx:7051, 7098` | Flat type folders keep today's graph usable until sub-project 2 replaces it |
| Rowboat knows one owner per workdir and sends everything under `knowledge/` to the LLM. It has no visibility filter | `note_creation.ts:44` | **One vault per tenant.** Private notes live outside company vaults |

From the business critique:

- Missing domains were legal and compliance, customer success, vendors, KPIs and decisions.
- Tenants and private data were not separated.
- People and organisations need one register, with their roles expressed as relations.
- Status must be a field, never a folder.

## 3. Vaults (tenancy and privacy)

| Vault (Rowboat workdir) | Contents | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.rowboat-<tenant>`, one per company or client (e.g. `vibemind`, `fin2gether`, `ehl`) | All business data of that tenant | That tenant's agents and team |
| `~/.rowboat-private` | Diary, applications, personal profile | The owner only. No company agent and no RAG index |

- Tenants never share a vault, so agents cannot read across tenants by design.
- Cross-tenant facts (e.g. one person working with two tenants) are duplicated on purpose, one note per
  vault, and linked by the same `id`.
- WP3's Qdrant index and every bridge must be configured per vault.

## 4. Levels and domains

Every note has a `level`:

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **L0** | The company: one note, `Company.md` |
| **L1** | Domain |
| **L2** | Area |
| **L3** | Entity: what you decide or act on |
| **L4** | Detail or evidence |

Domain and area are notes themselves, in `Domains/` and `Areas/`, so that every level is a real parent
in the tree.

### Business domains (L1) with areas (L2) and entity types (L3/L4)

| # | Domain (`domain:`) | Areas (L2) | Note types (folder) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `strategy` – Strategy & steering | Goals, KPIs, Decisions, Risks | `OKRs`, `KPIs`, `Decisions`, `Risks` |
| 2 | `legal` – Legal & compliance | Contracts, Data protection, AI Act, IP & licences | `Contracts`, `Processing Records`, `AI Systems`, `Licences` |
| 3 | `finance` – Finance & funding | Budget, Invoices, Funding, Pricing | `Budgets`, `Invoices`, `Funding`, `Price Plans` |
| 4 | `team` – Team & HR | Roles, Recruiting, Onboarding | `Roles`, `Candidates` |
| 5 | `sales` – Market & sales | Segments, Pipeline, Competitors | `Segments`, `Leads`, `Deals`, `Competitors` |
| 6 | `success` – Customer success & support | Onboarding, Support, Feedback, Design partners | `Tickets`, `Feedback` |
| 7 | `partners` – Partners & vendors | Partnerships, Vendors (LLM, SaaS, hosting) | `Partnerships`, `Vendors` |
| 8 | `marketing` – Marketing & brand | Brand, Campaigns, Content, Channels | `Brands`, `Campaigns`, `Content`, `Assets` |
| 9 | `product` – Product & engineering | Products, Roadmap, Requirements, Releases, Incidents | `Products`, `Models`, `Components`, `Feature Classes`, `Requirements`, `Purchase Drivers`, `Releases`, `Incidents` |
| 10 | `ai` – AI & agents | Agents, Workflows, Models & evals, Datasets, Compute | `Agents`, `Workflows`, `AI Models`, `Evals`, `Datasets` |
| 11 | `delivery` – Projects & delivery | Client projects, Initiatives, Milestones | `Projects` (built-in), `Milestones`, `Tasks`, `Initiatives` |
| 12 | `operations` – Operations & IT | Infrastructure, Tools, Security, Runbooks | `Systems`, `Tools`, `Runbooks` |

### Cross-cutting domains (also L1, so the tree stays complete)

| # | Domain | Note types | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | `register` – People & organisations | `People`, `Organizations` (built-in) | **Identity only, once.** Roles are relations (`works_at`, `contact_at`, `investor_in`, `candidate_for`) |
| 14 | `sources` – Raw inputs | `Meetings` (built-in), `Mails`, `Chats`, `Voice Memos`, `Agent Notes` | Parent is a date bucket (`Areas/Sources 2026-10`). Entities are linked through `about` |
| 15 | `knowledge` – Knowledge & evidence | `Topics` (built-in), `Studies`, `Data`, `Assumptions` | Evidence for decisions. Linked through `evidence` |

### Parent rules

1. The parent is **who owns and decides**. Examples:
   - A requirement hangs under its product or model.
   - A paid client project hangs under `Areas/Client projects`, with `customer:` and `product:` as relations.
2. **Identity and role are separate.** A person exists once in `People/`. That they are an employee, a
   customer contact or an investor is a relation, never a second note.
3. **Agents:**
   - The agent's definition lives in `Agents/`, domain `ai`.
   - What an agent did hangs under the object it worked on, with `executed_by:`.
4. **Status is a field.** No `Veraltet/` or `Archive/` folders. Use `status: archived`.

## 5. Filesystem

```
knowledge/
  Company.md                      L0
  Domains/   Strategy.md … Knowledge.md        L1 (15 notes)
  Areas/     Contracts.md, Pipeline.md, …      L2
  People/ Organizations/ Projects/ Topics/ Meetings/ Agent Notes/ Voice Memos/   Rowboat built-ins, unchanged
  OKRs/ KPIs/ Decisions/ Risks/ Contracts/ … Runbooks/                            one flat folder per type
```

- **One folder per note type, directly under `knowledge/`.** No nesting by domain.
- Folder names are English plurals, matching Rowboat's built-ins.
- File name = note title. The file name never changes once other notes link to it.

## 6. Front matter (every note)

Flat YAML, keys in `snake_case`. Links are always quoted and always use the full path `Type/Name`.

```yaml
---
id: org-acme                     # stable slug, never changes, unique per vault
type: Organizations              # = folder = notes.json type
domain: register
level: 3
parent: "[[Areas/Customers]]"
status: active                   # active | planning | on-hold | done | archived
visibility: team                 # team | restricted (no 'private': private data lives in the private vault)
env: prod                        # prod | test (smoke tests and fakes)
# typed relations: one key each, always a list of links
works_at: []
contact_at: []
customer: []
project: ["[[Projects/EHL 2026]]"]
product: []
owner: ["[[People/Felix Baumann]]"]
about: []
evidence: []
executed_by: []
when: 2026-10-12
```

### Relations (11)

| `contact_at` | Organizations | Person → customer or partner |
| `investor_in` / `candidate_for` | Organizations / Roles | Person → company / open role |
| `customer` | Organizations | Deal, project, ticket → customer |
| `project` | Projects | Task, mail, campaign → project |
| `product` | Products, Models | Requirement, release, project → product |
| `owner` | People, Agents | Anything → who is responsible |
| `about` | any | Mail, meeting, feedback → what it is about |
| `evidence` | Studies, Data, Topics, Meetings | Requirement, decision → its sources |

## 7. Schema as code (single source)

```
schema/
  vault-schema.yaml      domains, areas, levels, types (folder, domain, level, allowed parent types,
                         required relations, template body), relations, schema_version
  build.py               writes <workdir>/config/notes.json (template with the front matter block,
                         extractionGuide with the parent and relation rules) and
                         knowledge/Agent Notes/Vault Schema.md (readable rules for every agent)
  lint.py                checks a vault; exit code ≠ 0 on errors
  migrate.py             adds front matter to existing notes (dry run by default, writes a diff)
  tests/                 pytest
```

**`lint.py` checks:**

- YAML parses and the keys are flat.
- `type` matches the folder.
- `id` is unique.
- `parent` exists, has an allowed type and a lower level, and the tree has no cycles.
- Required relations are present.
- Every `[[link]]` resolves to an existing path (exact match).
- Possible duplicates: same normalised name or same email/domain in `People/` and `Organizations/`.

**`migrate.py`:**

1. Proposes `domain`, `level` and `parent` per note. The type comes from the schema. The parent comes from
   the existing links: the linked note of the highest allowed parent type.
2. Writes them only after review.
3. Never renames files.

**EHL vault** (`~/.rowboat-ehl`, ~190 notes):

| Folder | Domain |
|---|---|
| Brands | marketing |
| Models, Components, Feature Classes, Requirements, Purchase Drivers | product |
| Assumptions, Topics, Data | knowledge |
| Projects | delivery |

Parents:

- Model → Brand
- Component → its first model
- Feature Class → its component
- Requirement and Purchase Driver → their model

**VibeMind vault** (`~/.rowboat`):

| Folder | Domain / target |
|---|---|
| Agents/ | ai: `Agents` (`Veraltet/` → `status: archived`) |
| Workflows/ | ai: `Workflows` |
| Videos/ | marketing: `Assets` (eval runs → ai: `Evals`) |
| Bubbles/ | delivery: `Initiatives` (smoke tests → `env: test`) |
| Projects/ | delivery (requirement gaps → product: `Requirements`) |
| Topics/ | knowledge |
| Hubs/ | `Areas` |
| Investor Programs/ | finance: `Funding` |
| Notes/Traction Metrics | strategy: `KPIs` |
| System/ | operations: `Systems` |
| People/Design Partners | register: `Organizations` + success |
| companys/<Firma>/ | per-tenant vault: marketing `Brands` |
| Diary/, Bewerbung/, User_Profile | → **`~/.rowboat-private`** |

**Sales-Claw** (via the bridge, sub-project 4):

| Source | Target |
|---|---|
| leads | `People` + `Organizations` (register) + `Leads` (sales) |
| personas | `Segments` |
| activities | `Agent Notes`/sources, with `about` |

- Drafts, consent and block list (`compliance.sperrliste`) **stay in Sales-Claw**. Personal data that is not
  needed is never copied.

**Marketing** (via the bridge):

| Source | Target |
|---|---|
| Campaigns, contents | `Campaigns`, `Content` |
| Crowdfunding | `Funding` |
| Mandanten | one vault each |
| Send orders | stay in Marketing/Sales-Claw (spec D7: we never send) |

## 9. Out of scope

- **Payroll, bank data, full HR files.** The vault only holds references, such as "contract signed, see HR
  system".
- **Moving data between the existing vaults.** This spec only defines the target. Moving the VibeMind
  vault is a separate, manual step after review.
- **Sub-projects 2–4:**
  - 3D view in Rowboat.
  - Agents writing the fields.
  - Bridges for Sales-Claw and Marketing.

   from the schema only)? Real notes are visible and linkable; virtual ones keep the vault smaller.

Die drei Durchgänge sind fertig. Das Ergebnis steht als Spec-Entwurf in [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md), gepusht auf dem Branch `feat/vault-schema`.

## Was die Durchgänge verändert haben
1. **Entwurf:** 11 Domänen, und die Hierarchie sollte über Unterordner laufen (Domäne/Typ/Notiz).
2. **Zwei Kritiken.** Die wichtigsten Befunde:
   - **Unterordner gehen in Rowboat kaputt.** Seine Agenten schreiben fest nach `People/` und `Organizations/`, Links funktionieren nur über den exakten Pfad, und beim Umbenennen eines Ordners zerbrechen alle Links darunter.
   - Rowboats Eigenschaften-Editor **löscht verschachteltes YAML**.
   - Rowboat schickt den ganzen Vault ans LLM. **Private Notizen** wie Diary und Bewerbung und **verschiedene Mandanten** gehören deshalb nicht in denselben Vault.
   - Es fehlten Recht & Compliance, Support, Lieferanten, KPIs und Entscheidungen.
3. **Endfassung:**
   - **Ein Vault pro Mandant**, dazu ein privater Vault außerhalb der Firma.
   - **15 Domänen auf L1:** 12 Geschäftsdomänen (Strategie, Recht & Compliance, **Finanzen**, Team & HR, Vertrieb, Kundenerfolg, Partner & Lieferanten, Marketing, Produkt, KI & Agenten, Projekte, Betrieb & IT) und 3 übergreifende (Register für Personen und Firmen, Rohquellen, Wissen & Belege).
   - **Ordner bleiben flach, einer pro Typ**, wie Rowboat es erwartet. Die Hierarchie steckt im **flachen Frontmatter**: `id`, `type`, `domain`, `level`, `parent`, dazu 11 benannte Beziehungen, jede als eigener Schlüssel.
   - **Das Schema ist Code:** `schema/vault-schema.yaml` als einzige Quelle. Ein Generator erzeugt daraus `notes.json` und eine Regel-Notiz für die Agenten. Ein Prüfskript läuft in CI, ein Migrationsskript arbeitet standardmäßig im Probelauf.
   - **Bestehende Daten sind zugeordnet:** der EHL-Vault, dein VibeMind-Vault Ordner für Ordner, Sales-Claw und Marketing.

## Zwei offene Punkte (Abschnitt 10)
1. Sollen L0–L2 (Firma, Domänen, Bereiche) **echte Notizen** sein, sichtbar und verlinkbar, oder nur **virtuell** aus dem Schema berechnet?
2. **Finanzen:** echte Beträge im Vault oder nur Verweise aufs Buchhaltungssystem?

Lies die Spec bitte gegen und beantworte die beiden Fragen. Danach schreibe ich den Umsetzungsplan für Teilprojekt 1.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**

Only notes with "managed_by: torque" in their front matter are ever rewritten; delete that line to keep a note

# Vault Schema Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build `schema/`, a single-source vault schema with a generator, a linter and a migration, and
move the EHL vault (`~/.rowboat-ehl`) onto it.

**Architecture:** `schema/vault-schema.yaml` is the only place that defines domains, areas, note types
and relations. A small Python package `ehl_schema` loads it and uses it in three commands:

- `build` writes the structure notes (Company, Domains, Areas), Rowboat's `config/notes.json` and a
  rules note for agents.
- `lint` checks every note of a vault.
- `migrate` adds the missing front matter keys to existing notes. It only proposes changes unless you
  pass `--write`.

Folders stay flat, one per type, as Rowboat expects. The hierarchy lives in flat YAML front matter.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, PyYAML, pytest, GitHub Actions. It runs in `market/.venv`, which the
installer already creates and which already has PyYAML and pytest.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- **Language and dependencies:**
  - Python `>=3.12`, own `pyproject.toml` in `schema/`.
  - Only runtime dependency: `pyyaml>=6`.
  - Tests: pytest.
- **Logging:** use `logging`, never `print`.
- **Platforms:** everything runs on Windows and macOS. Read files as UTF-8 and accept CRLF and a BOM.
- **Front matter:**
  - Flat YAML only: every value is a scalar or a list of strings.
  - Links are always quoted, full path: `parent: "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"`, `customer: ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]`.
- **Files:** never rename or move a note file. Never rewrite a key a note already has. Existing front
  matter lines stay first and unchanged; new keys are appended.
- **Generated notes:** they carry `managed_by: schema`. Only those are ever rewritten by `build`.
- **Rowboat stays unmodified.** We only write `<workdir>/config/notes.json` and notes in `<workdir>/knowledge/`.
- **Never commit a vault (`~/.rowboat*`) or its notes** (CLAUDE.md data rules).
- **Commits:** Conventional commits ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Python interpreter in commands:** `market/.venv/Scripts/python` (Windows) or `market/.venv/bin/python`
  (macOS). The commands below use the Windows form.

## Review Focus

1. **Windows files with CRLF and a BOM.**
   - The notes written by `brand.py` on Windows are CRLF.
   - Front matter must still parse, and a migrated file must keep its CRLF.
   - Test: Task 2 `test_split_accepts_bom_and_crlf`, `test_add_keys_keeps_crlf_and_existing_lines`.
2. **Note names with `&`, commas, brackets, umlauts, and links with alias, heading or attachment.**
   - `[[Brands/BMW|BMW]]`, `[[Models/5er G60#Sales]]` and `[[Data/BMW Dataset.xlsx]]` must resolve.
   - `Badges & logos` must round-trip through YAML.
   - Test: Task 2 `test_links_strip_alias_and_heading`, `test_format_value_round_trips`; Task 3
     `test_alias_and_attachment_links_resolve`.
3. **Re-running is harmless.**
   - A second `build` writes nothing.
   - The schema rules are not appended to `notes.json` twice.
   - A second `migrate` proposes nothing.
   - Test: Task 4 `test_build_is_idempotent`; Task 5 `test_migrate_is_idempotent`.
4. **Existing front matter survives.**
   - `managed_by: torque` must stay within the first 300 characters (`demo/torque/sync.py` checks `old[:300]`).
   - Unknown keys (`part_id`, `req_id`) are untouched.
   - Torque's sync must not drop the new keys when it rewrites a note.
   - Test: Task 2 `test_add_keys_keeps_crlf_and_existing_lines`; Task 7 `test_write_if_changed_keeps_schema_keys`.
5. **Mutual links between notes of the same type** (`Projects/G60` ↔ `Projects/G60 Roadmap`) must not
   produce an inverted parent or a cycle.
   - Test: Task 5 `test_plan_chooses_parents`, which also covers the incoming-link case
     (driver → its top 10 note).

## File Structure

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `schema/pyproject.toml` | Package `ehl-schema`, dependency, script entry |
| `schema/vault-schema.yaml` | The schema: domains, areas, relations, types |
| `schema/ehl_schema/__init__.py` | Package marker |
| `schema/ehl_schema/model.py` | Load and check the schema → `Schema`, `TypeDef`, `RelationDef` |
| `schema/ehl_schema/notes.py` | Read a vault; split, format and extend front matter; parse links |
| `schema/ehl_schema/lint.py` | `lint(schema, vault) -> list[Issue]` |
| `schema/ehl_schema/build.py` | Structure notes, rules note, `notes.json` |
| `schema/ehl_schema/migrate.py` | `plan`, `apply` and `diff` for missing front matter |
| `schema/ehl_schema/cli.py` | `python -m ehl_schema.cli build|lint|migrate` |
| `schema/tests/helpers.py` | Test helpers: write notes, build small vaults |
| `schema/tests/test_*.py` | One test file per module |
| `demo/torque/sync.py` (modify) | Keep foreign front matter keys on rewrite |
| `demo/tests/test_sync_frontmatter.py` | Test for that |
| `scripts/install.py` (modify) | Install the package; run build, migrate and lint after the vault notes |
| `.github/workflows/schema.yml` | CI: run `schema/tests` |
| `README.md`, the spec (modify) | Document `schema/`; record the parent rule and the channel areas |

---

### Task 1: Package, schema file and schema loader

**Files:**
- Create: `schema/pyproject.toml`, `schema/vault-schema.yaml`, `schema/ehl_schema/__init__.py`, `schema/ehl_schema/model.py`
- Test: `schema/tests/test_model.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `DEFAULT_SCHEMA: Path`
  - `STRUCTURE_TYPES = ("Company", "Domains", "Areas")`
  - `class SchemaError(ValueError)`
  - `TypeDef(name, domain, level, parent: tuple[str, ...], default_parent: str | None, builtin: bool, required: tuple[str, ...], optional: tuple[str, ...], statuses: tuple[str, ...], template: str | None)`
  - `RelationDef(name, targets: tuple[str, ...] | None, kind: str)`
  - `Schema(version: int, domains: dict[str, str], cross_cutting: frozenset[str], areas: dict[str, str], relations: dict[str, RelationDef], types: dict[str, TypeDef])` with methods:
    - `domain_note(key) -> str` (`"Domains/<title>"`)
    - `area_note(name) -> str` (`"Areas/<name>"`)
    - `domain_key(title) -> str | None`
    - `type_of_path(path) -> str | None`
  - `load_schema(path: Path = DEFAULT_SCHEMA) -> Schema`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the package files**

`schema/pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "ehl-schema"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Vault schema: one hierarchy for all business data (build, lint, migrate)"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["pyyaml>=6"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]

[project.scripts]
ehl-schema = "ehl_schema.cli:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["ehl_schema*"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
```

`schema/ehl_schema/__init__.py`:

```python
"""Vault schema: one hierarchy for all business data of a company (see schema/vault-schema.yaml)."""
```

`schema/vault-schema.yaml`:


```python
"""Load the vault schema (schema/vault-schema.yaml) and check that it is consistent."""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.model")

DEFAULT_SCHEMA = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "vault-schema.yaml"
STRUCTURE_TYPES = ("Company", "Domains", "Areas")


class SchemaError(ValueError):
    """The schema file is malformed or contradicts itself."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TypeDef:
    name: str
    domain: str                      # domain key; "*" for the generated structure types
    level: int                       # 0 Company, 1 Domains, 2 Areas, 3 entity, 4 detail
    parent: tuple[str, ...]          # allowed parent types, in order of preference
    default_parent: str | None = None  # area name used when no linked note fits
    builtin: bool = False            # a Rowboat type: keep its template body
    required: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    optional: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    statuses: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    template: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RelationDef:
    name: str
    targets: tuple[str, ...] | None  # None = any note type
    kind: str = "link"               # "link" or "date"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Schema:
    version: int
    domains: dict[str, str]          # key -> title
    cross_cutting: frozenset[str]
    areas: dict[str, str]            # area name -> domain key
    relations: dict[str, RelationDef]
    types: dict[str, TypeDef]

    def domain_note(self, key: str) -> str:
        return f"Domains/{self.domains[key]}"

    def area_note(self, name: str) -> str:
        return f"Areas/{name}"

    def domain_key(self, title: str) -> str | None:
        return next((k for k, t in self.domains.items() if t == title), None)

    def type_of_path(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        """Schema type of a vault-relative note path without '.md', or None if the schema does not know it."""
        if path == "Company":
            return "Company"
        folder, sep, _ = path.partition("/")
        return folder if sep and folder in self.types else None


def _structure_types() -> dict[str, TypeDef]:
    return {
        "Company": TypeDef("Company", "*", 0, ()),
        "Domains": TypeDef("Domains", "*", 1, ("Company",)),
        "Areas": TypeDef("Areas", "*", 2, ("Domains",)),
    }


def load_schema(path: Path = DEFAULT_SCHEMA) -> Schema:
    raw = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise SchemaError(f"{path}: the schema must be a mapping")
    try:
        domains = {str(k): str(v["title"]) for k, v in raw["domains"].items()}
        cross = frozenset(str(k) for k, v in raw["domains"].items() if v.get("cross_cutting"))
        areas = {str(k): str(v) for k, v in raw["areas"].items()}
        relations = {}
        for name, spec in raw["relations"].items():
            spec = spec or {}
            targets = spec.get("targets")
            relations[str(name)] = RelationDef(
                str(name), None if targets in (None, "any") else tuple(targets), spec.get("kind", "link"))
        types = _structure_types()
        for name, spec in raw["types"].items():
            if name in types:
                raise SchemaError(f"type {name!r} is reserved for the generated structure notes")
            types[str(name)] = TypeDef(
                name=str(name), domain=str(spec["domain"]), level=int(spec["level"]),
                parent=tuple(spec["parent"]), default_parent=spec.get("default_parent"),
                builtin=bool(spec.get("builtin", False)), required=tuple(spec.get("required", ())),
                optional=tuple(spec.get("optional", ())), statuses=tuple(spec.get("statuses", ())),
                template=spec.get("template"))
        schema = Schema(int(raw["schema_version"]), domains, cross, areas, relations, types)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as err:
        raise SchemaError(f"{path}: malformed schema ({err!r})") from err
    _check(schema)
    return schema


def _check(schema: Schema) -> None:
    errors = []
    for area, domain in schema.areas.items():
        if domain not in schema.domains:
            errors.append(f"area {area!r}: unknown domain {domain!r}")
    for key in schema.domains:
        if key not in schema.areas.values():
            errors.append(f"domain {key!r} has no area")
    for rel in schema.relations.values():
        if rel.kind not in ("link", "date"):
            errors.append(f"relation {rel.name!r}: kind must be link or date")
        for target in rel.targets or ():
            if target not in schema.types:
                errors.append(f"relation {rel.name!r}: unknown target type {target!r}")
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
            continue
        if td.domain not in schema.domains:
            errors.append(f"type {name!r}: unknown domain {td.domain!r}")
        if td.level not in (3, 4):
            errors.append(f"type {name!r}: level must be 3 or 4")
        if not td.parent:
            errors.append(f"type {name!r}: parent must list at least one type")
        for parent in td.parent:
            if parent not in schema.types or parent in ("Company", "Domains"):
                errors.append(f"type {name!r}: {parent!r} is not an allowed parent")
        if td.default_parent is not None and td.default_parent not in schema.areas:
            errors.append(f"type {name!r}: unknown default_parent {td.default_parent!r}")
        for rel in td.required + td.optional:
            if rel not in schema.relations:
                errors.append(f"type {name!r}: unknown relation {rel!r}")
    if errors:
        raise SchemaError("\n".join(errors))
```

```python
"""Vault notes: read a vault, split and extend flat front matter, parse [[links]]."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

LINK = re.compile(r"\[\[([^\]\n]+)\]\]")
PLAIN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*")
DATE = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")
RESERVED = {"true", "false", "yes", "no", "on", "off", "null", "none", "y", "n"}


class FrontMatterError(ValueError):
    """The front matter is not valid YAML or not a mapping."""


@dataclass
class Note:
    path: str                 # vault-relative, forward slashes, without ".md"
    raw: str                  # the file as read (decoded, original newlines)
    front: dict | None        # parsed front matter; None if the note has none (or it is broken)
    front_text: str           # the lines between the --- fences, "\n"-separated
    body: str                 # everything after the closing fence, "\n" newlines
    newline: str              # "\r\n" or "\n", as found in the file
    error: str | None = None  # why the front matter could not be read


def _normalise(value):
    if isinstance(value, (date, datetime)):
        return value.isoformat()[:10]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_normalise(v) for v in value]
    return value


def split(text: str) -> tuple[dict | None, str, str]:
    """(front matter or None, raw front matter lines, body). Accepts a BOM and CRLF."""
    t = text.lstrip("﻿").replace("\r\n", "\n")
    if not t.startswith("---\n"):
        return None, "", t
    if t.startswith("---\n---\n"):
        return {}, "", t[8:]
    end = t.find("\n---\n", 3)
    if end == -1:
        if t.endswith("\n---"):
            end = len(t) - 4
        else:
            return None, "", t
    raw = t[4:end]
    body = t[end + 5:]
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
    except yaml.YAMLError as err:
        raise FrontMatterError(f"front matter is not valid YAML: {err}") from err
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise FrontMatterError("front matter is not a mapping")
    return {str(k): _normalise(v) for k, v in data.items()}, raw, body


def format_value(value) -> str:
    """One YAML value as it is written into front matter: plain when safe, JSON-quoted otherwise."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return json.dumps([str(v) for v in value], ensure_ascii=False)
    text = str(value)
    if DATE.fullmatch(text) or (PLAIN.fullmatch(text) and text.lower() not in RESERVED):
        return text
    return json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False)


def render_front(fields: dict) -> str:
    return "\n".join(f"{key}: {format_value(value)}" for key, value in fields.items())


def note_text(fields: dict, body: str) -> str:
    return f"---\n{render_front(fields)}\n---\n{body}"


def add_keys(note: Note, fields: dict) -> str:
    """The note's text with every key of `fields` it does not have yet appended to its front matter.
    Existing lines stay first and unchanged; the file's newline style is kept."""
    existing = note.front or {}
    lines = [line for line in note.front_text.split("\n") if line.strip()] if note.front is not None else []
    lines += [f"{key}: {format_value(value)}" for key, value in fields.items() if key not in existing]
    text = "---\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n---\n" + note.body
    return text.replace("\n", "\r\n") if note.newline == "\r\n" else text


def link_target(raw: str) -> str:
    return raw.split("|", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0].strip()


def links(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return [t for t in (link_target(m) for m in LINK.findall(text)) if t]


def link_value(value) -> str | None:
    """Target of a value that is exactly one [[link]], else None."""
    m = LINK.fullmatch(value.strip()) if isinstance(value, str) else None
    return link_target(m.group(1)) if m else None


def parent_target(note: Note) -> str | None:
    return link_value((note.front or {}).get("parent"))


def read_vault(vault: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Note], set[str]]:
    """All notes (path without .md -> Note) and all file paths; skips hidden folders such as .git."""
    notes: dict[str, Note] = {}
    files: set[str] = set()
    for file in sorted(vault.rglob("*")):
        rel = file.relative_to(vault)
        if not file.is_file() or any(part.startswith(".") for part in rel.parts):
            continue
        key = rel.as_posix()
        files.add(key)
        if file.suffix != ".md":
            continue
        raw = file.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
        newline = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
        try:
            front, front_text, body = split(raw)
            error = None
        except FrontMatterError as err:
            front, front_text, body, error = None, "", raw.replace("\r\n", "\n"), str(err)
        notes[key[:-3]] = Note(key[:-3], raw, front, front_text, body, newline, error)
    return notes, files


def slug(text: str) -> str:
    ascii_text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")
```

```python
"""Check a vault against the schema. Errors break the hierarchy; warnings are worth a look."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from .model import Schema, TypeDef
from .notes import DATE, Note, link_value, links, parent_target, read_vault

FIELD = re.compile(r"^\*\*(Email|Domain):\*\*\s*(\S+)", re.M)
BASE_KEYS = ("id", "type", "domain", "level")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Issue:
    severity: str   # "error" | "warning"
    path: str
    code: str
    message: str


def errors(issues: list[Issue]) -> list[Issue]:
    return [i for i in issues if i.severity == "error"]


def lint(schema: Schema, vault: Path) -> list[Issue]:
    notes, files = read_vault(vault)
    issues: list[Issue] = []
    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
    for note in notes.values():
        issues.extend(_check_note(schema, note, notes, files, ids))
    issues.extend(_check_cycles(notes))
    issues.extend(_check_duplicates(notes))
    return sorted(issues, key=lambda i: (i.path, i.code, i.message))


def _expected_domain(schema: Schema, tname: str, path: str) -> str | None:
    name = path.partition("/")[2]
    if tname == "Domains":
        return schema.domain_key(name)
    if tname == "Areas":
        return schema.areas.get(name)
    return schema.types[tname].domain


def _check_note(schema: Schema, note: Note, notes: dict, files: set, ids: dict) -> list[Issue]:
    out: list[Issue] = []

    def add(severity: str, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        out.append(Issue(severity, note.path, code, message))

    tname = schema.type_of_path(note.path)
    if tname is None:
        add("error", "unknown-type", "the folder of this note is not a note type in the schema")
        return out
    if note.error:
        add("error", "bad-yaml", note.error)
        return out
    if note.front is None:
        add("error", "no-front-matter", "the note has no front matter (run: ehl-schema migrate)")
        return out
    front = note.front
    for key, value in front.items():
        if isinstance(value, dict) or (isinstance(value, list) and not all(isinstance(v, str) for v in value)):
            add("error", "nested", f"{key!r} must be flat: a value or a list of strings")
    needed = BASE_KEYS + (() if tname == "Company" else ("parent",))
    for key in needed:
        if front.get(key) in (None, ""):
            add("error", "missing-key", f"{key!r} is missing")
    if out:
        return out
    td = schema.types[tname]
    if front["type"] != tname:
        add("error", "type-mismatch", f"type is {front['type']!r}, but the folder says {tname!r}")
    if tname != "Company":
        expected = _expected_domain(schema, tname, note.path)
        if expected is None:
            add("error", "not-in-schema", f"{note.path!r} is not a domain or area of the schema")
        elif front["domain"] != expected:
            add("error", "domain-mismatch", f"domain is {front['domain']!r}, expected {expected!r}")
    if front["level"] != td.level:
        add("error", "level-mismatch", f"level is {front['level']!r}, expected {td.level}")
    first = ids.setdefault(str(front["id"]), note.path)
    if first != note.path:
        add("error", "duplicate-id", f"id {front['id']!r} is also used by {first!r}")
    if tname != "Company":
        out.extend(_check_parent(schema, note, td, notes))
    out.extend(_check_relations(schema, note, td, notes, files))
    if td.statuses and "status" in front and front["status"] not in td.statuses:
        add("warning", "status-value", f"status {front['status']!r} is not one of {', '.join(td.statuses)}")
    for target in links(note.body):
        if target not in notes and target not in files:
            add("warning", "broken-link", f"[[{target}]] does not exist")
    return out


def _check_parent(schema: Schema, note: Note, td: TypeDef, notes: dict) -> list[Issue]:
    target = parent_target(note)
    if target is None:
        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-format", 'parent must be one quoted link like "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"')]
    if target not in notes:
        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-missing", f"parent [[{target}]] does not exist")]
    ptype = schema.type_of_path(target)
    if ptype not in td.parent:
        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-type",
                      f"parent [[{target}]] is a {ptype}; allowed: {', '.join(td.parent)}")]
    if schema.types[ptype].level > td.level:
        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-level", f"parent [[{target}]] is on a lower level than the note")]
    return []


def _check_relations(schema: Schema, note: Note, td: TypeDef, notes: dict, files: set) -> list[Issue]:
    out: list[Issue] = []
    front = note.front or {}
    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
        if name not in front:
            if name in td.required:
                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "required-relation", f"{name!r} is required"))
            continue
        value = front[name]
        if rel.kind == "date":
            if not isinstance(value, str) or not DATE.fullmatch(value):
                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-format", f"{name!r} must be a date YYYY-MM-DD"))
            continue
        targets = [link_value(v) for v in value] if isinstance(value, list) else [None]
        if None in targets:
            out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-format",
                             f'{name!r} must be a list of quoted links like ["[[Folder/Name]]"]'))
            continue
        if not targets and name in td.required:
            out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "required-relation", f"{name!r} must not be empty"))
        for target in targets:
            if target not in notes and target not in files:
                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-missing", f"{name}: [[{target}]] does not exist"))
            elif rel.targets is not None and schema.type_of_path(target) not in rel.targets:
                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-target",
                                 f"{name}: [[{target}]] must be a {' or '.join(rel.targets)}"))
    return out


def _check_cycles(notes: dict[str, Note]) -> list[Issue]:
    parent = {p: t for p, n in notes.items() if (t := parent_target(n)) is not None}
    out, reported = [], set()
    for start in parent:
        seen, node = [], start
        while node in parent and node not in seen:
            seen.append(node)
            node = parent[node]
        if node in seen:
            cycle = seen[seen.index(node):]
            key = frozenset(cycle)
            if key not in reported:
                reported.add(key)
                out.append(Issue("error", min(cycle), "cycle", "parent chain loops: " + " -> ".join(cycle + [node])))
    return out


def _check_duplicates(notes: dict[str, Note]) -> list[Issue]:
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
    for path, note in notes.items():
        folder, _, name = path.partition("/")
        if folder not in ("People", "Organizations") or not name:
            continue
        keys = {("name", folder + ":" + re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", name.lower()))}
        for kind, value in FIELD.findall(note.body):
            value = value.strip().lower()
            if value and not value.startswith("{"):
                keys.add((kind.lower(), value))
        for key in keys:
            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(path)
    out = []
    for (kind, _), paths in groups.items():
        if len(paths) > 1:
            for path in paths:
                others = ", ".join(p for p in paths if p != path)
                out.append(Issue("warning", path, "possible-duplicate", f"same {kind} as {others}"))
    return out
```

```python
"""Generate what the schema implies: Company/Domains/Areas notes, the rules note and Rowboat's notes.json."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path

from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, TypeDef
from .notes import note_text, slug, split

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.build")

MANAGED = "schema"
RULES_NOTE = "Agent Notes/Vault Schema"
RULES_MARK = "\n\nSchema rules ("
GENERIC_BODY = ("# {Title}\n\n## Summary\n{2-3 sentences.}\n\n## Key facts\n{Substantive facts only. Leave empty if "
                "none.}\n\n## Open items\n{Next steps only. Leave empty if none.}\n")


def _front(schema: Schema, **fields) -> dict:
    return {**fields, "managed_by": MANAGED, "schema_version": schema.version}


def structure_notes(schema: Schema, company: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    notes: dict[str, str] = {}
    domain_links = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.domain_note(k)}]]" for k in schema.domains)
    notes["Company"] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="company", type="Company", domain="company", level=0),
        f"# {company}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Company (L0)\n\n## Domains\n{domain_links}\n")
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.area_note(a)}]]" for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        notes[schema.domain_note(key)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"domain-{key}", type="Domains", domain=key, level=1, parent="[[Company]]"),
            f"# {title}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Domain (L1)\n**Key:** {key}\n\n## Areas\n{areas}\n")
    for area, key in schema.areas.items():
        types = ", ".join(n for n, td in schema.types.items() if td.default_parent == area) or "none"
        notes[schema.area_note(area)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"area-{slug(area)}", type="Areas", domain=key, level=2,
                   parent=f"[[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]"),
            f"# {area}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Area (L2)\n**Domain:** [[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]\n"
            f"**Note types placed here by default:** {types}\n")
    td = schema.types["Agent Notes"]
    notes[RULES_NOTE] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="agent-notes-vault-schema", type="Agent Notes", domain=td.domain, level=td.level,
               parent=f"[[{schema.area_note(td.default_parent)}]]"),
        rules_body(schema))
    return notes


def rules_body(schema: Schema) -> str:
    lines = [f"# Vault schema (v{schema.version})", "",
             "Generated from schema/vault-schema.yaml by `ehl-schema build`. Do not edit; change the schema file.", "",
             "## Front matter", "",
             "Every note starts with flat YAML front matter. Required keys: id, type, domain, level, parent.",
             "- `id`: a stable slug; never change it. `type`: the folder name. `level`: from the table below.",
             '- `parent`: exactly one quoted link, for example `parent: "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"`.',
             '- Relations are lists of quoted links with the full path, for example `about: ["[[Areas/Pipeline]]"]`.',
             "- Never nest keys. Optional: status, visibility (team | restricted), env (prod | test), when (YYYY-MM-DD).",
             "", "## Domains and areas", "", "| Domain | Key | Areas |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = ", ".join(a for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        lines.append(f"| {title} | {key} | {areas} |")
    lines += ["", "## Note types", "",
              "| Type (folder) | Domain | Level | Parent (in order) | Default area | Required | Optional |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
            continue
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {td.domain} | {td.level} | {', '.join(td.parent)} | {td.default_parent or ''} | "
                     f"{', '.join(td.required) or '–'} | {', '.join(td.optional) or '–'} |")
    lines += ["", "## Relations", "", "| Key | Points to |", "|---|---|"]
    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
        target = "a date" if rel.kind == "date" else ("any note" if rel.targets is None else ", ".join(rel.targets))
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {target} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def write_structure(schema: Schema, vault: Path, company: str) -> int:
    written = 0
    for path, text in structure_notes(schema, company).items():
        file = vault / f"{path}.md"
        if file.exists():
            old = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            if old == text:
                continue
            front, _, _ = split(old)
            if (front or {}).get("managed_by") != MANAGED:
                log.warning("%s exists and is not managed by the schema; left as it is", file)
                continue
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written += 1
    return written


def _parent_hint(td: TypeDef) -> str:
    if td.parent == ("Areas",):
        return f"Areas/{td.default_parent}"
    options = ", ".join(f"{p}/…" for p in td.parent if p != "Areas")
    return f"one of: {options}" + (f" (else Areas/{td.default_parent})" if td.default_parent else "")


def _skeleton(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    lines = ["---", "id: {slug of the title}", f"type: {td.name}", f"domain: {td.domain}", f"level: {td.level}",
             f'parent: "[[{{{_parent_hint(td)}}}]]"']
    for name in td.required:
        rel = schema.relations[name]
        if rel.kind == "date":
            lines.append(f"{name}: {{YYYY-MM-DD}}")
        else:
            target = rel.targets[0] if rel.targets else "Folder"
            lines.append(f'{name}: ["[[{{{target}/…}}]]"]')
    lines += [f"schema_version: {schema.version}", "---", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _guide(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    default = f" (else [[Areas/{td.default_parent}]])" if td.default_parent else ""
    return (f"v{schema.version}): flat YAML front matter. type: {td.name}; domain: {td.domain}; level: {td.level}; "
            f"id: a stable slug, never change it. parent: exactly one quoted link to a note of type "
            f"{', '.join(td.parent)}{default}. Required relations: {', '.join(td.required) or 'none'}. "
            f"Optional relations: {', '.join(td.optional) or 'none'}. Relation values are lists of quoted "
            f'full-path links like ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]. Status: {", ".join(td.statuses) or "free text"}.')


def notes_json(schema: Schema, existing: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    by_type = {e["type"]: dict(e) for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e}
    order = [e["type"] for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES or (td.builtin and name not in by_type):
            continue
        entry = by_type.get(name, {"type": name, "folder": name, "template": "", "extractionGuide": ""})
        if name not in by_type:
            order.append(name)
        template = entry.get("template") or ""
        if not (td.builtin and not template.strip()):
            _, _, body = split(template)
            body = body if body.strip() else (td.template or GENERIC_BODY)
            entry["template"] = _skeleton(schema, td) + body
        guide = (entry.get("extractionGuide") or "").split(RULES_MARK)[0]
        entry["extractionGuide"] = guide + RULES_MARK + _guide(schema, td)
        by_type[name] = entry
    return [by_type[name] for name in order]


def build(schema: Schema, workdir: Path, company: str) -> dict:
    written = write_structure(schema, workdir / "knowledge", company)
    config = workdir / "config" / "notes.json"
    if not config.exists():
        log.warning("%s does not exist yet: start Rowboat once, then run build again", config)
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "missing"}
    old = config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    new = json.dumps(notes_json(schema, json.loads(old)), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
    if new == old:
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "unchanged"}
    config.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "updated"}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `schema/ehl_schema/migrate.py`
- Test: `schema/tests/test_migrate.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 1: `Schema`, `STRUCTURE_TYPES`
  - Task 2: `add_keys`, `links`, `parent_target`, `read_vault`, `slug`
  - Task 3: `lint`, `errors`
  - Task 4: `build`
- Produces:
  - `Report(changes: dict[str, tuple[str, str]], unmapped: list[str], unresolved: list[str])`
  - `plan(schema, vault: Path) -> Report`
  - `apply(report, vault: Path) -> int`
  - `diff(report) -> str`

**How a parent is chosen:**
- **Candidates:** the notes this note links to, plus the notes that link to it. Each candidate must
  exist, must not be the note itself, must have a type allowed as a parent, and must not be on a lower
  level than the note.
- **Same type (hub rule):** a candidate of the note's own type is only taken if it has more distinct
  neighbours than the note.
- **No cycles:** a candidate that would create a cycle is skipped.
- **Ranking:** first by the position of its type in `parent`, then by more neighbours, then by path.
- **Fallback:** `Areas/<default_parent>`. If there is no default either, the note is reported as unresolved.
- **Processing order:** by level, then by more neighbours, then by path.

```python
"""Give existing notes the schema's front matter keys. Proposes changes; writes only through apply()."""
from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, TypeDef
from .notes import Note, add_keys, links, parent_target, read_vault, slug

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.migrate")


@dataclass
class Report:
    changes: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # path -> (old text, new text)
    unmapped: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)   # notes in folders the schema does not know
    unresolved: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # no parent found and no default area


def _neighbours(notes: dict[str, Note]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
    out = {path: set() for path in notes}
    for path, note in notes.items():
        for target in links(note.front_text + "\n" + note.body):
            if target in notes and target != path:
                out[path].add(target)
                out[target].add(path)
    return out


def _creates_cycle(child: str, candidate: str, parents: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    node, steps = candidate, 0
    while node is not None and steps <= len(parents):
        if node == child:
            return True
        node = parents.get(node)
        steps += 1
    return False


def _choose_parent(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef, path: str, notes: dict, near: dict, parents: dict) -> str | None:
    best = None
    for candidate in near[path]:
        ctype = schema.type_of_path(candidate)
        if ctype not in td.parent or schema.types[ctype].level > td.level:
            continue
        if ctype == td.name and len(near[candidate]) <= len(near[path]):
            continue
        if _creates_cycle(path, candidate, parents):
            continue
        rank = (td.parent.index(ctype), -len(near[candidate]), candidate)
        if best is None or rank < best[0]:
            best = (rank, candidate)
    if best is not None:
        return best[1]
    return schema.area_note(td.default_parent) if td.default_parent else None


def _unique_id(base: str, used: set[str]) -> str:
    candidate, n = base, 1
    while candidate in used:
        n += 1
        candidate = f"{base}-{n}"
    used.add(candidate)
    return candidate


def plan(schema: Schema, vault: Path) -> Report:
    notes, _ = read_vault(vault)
    near = _neighbours(notes)
    parents = {p: t for p, n in notes.items() if (t := parent_target(n)) is not None}
    used_ids = {str(n.front["id"]) for n in notes.values() if n.front and n.front.get("id")}
    report = Report()
    todo = []
    for path, note in notes.items():
        tname = schema.type_of_path(path)
        if tname is None:
            report.unmapped.append(path)
        elif tname not in STRUCTURE_TYPES and note.error is None:
            todo.append((schema.types[tname].level, -len(near[path]), path))
    for _, _, path in sorted(todo):
        note, td = notes[path], schema.types[schema.type_of_path(path)]
        front = note.front or {}
        fields: dict = {}
        if not front.get("parent"):
            target = _choose_parent(schema, td, path, notes, near, parents)
            if target is None:
                report.unresolved.append(path)
                continue
            parents[path] = target
        if not front.get("id"):
            fields["id"] = _unique_id(slug(f"{td.name}-{path.partition('/')[2]}"), used_ids)
        fields.update({"type": td.name, "domain": td.domain, "level": td.level})
        if path in parents and not front.get("parent"):
            fields["parent"] = f"[[{parents[path]}]]"
        fields.update({"visibility": "team", "env": "prod", "schema_version": schema.version})
        new = add_keys(note, {k: v for k, v in fields.items() if k not in front})
        if new != note.raw:
            report.changes[path] = (note.raw, new)
    return report


def apply(report: Report, vault: Path) -> int:
    for path, (_, new) in report.changes.items():
        (vault / f"{path}.md").write_bytes(new.encode("utf-8"))
    return len(report.changes)


def diff(report: Report) -> str:
    parts = []
    for path, (old, new) in report.changes.items():
        parts.extend(difflib.unified_diff(old.replace("\r\n", "\n").splitlines(keepends=True),
                                          new.replace("\r\n", "\n").splitlines(keepends=True),
                                          f"a/{path}.md", f"b/{path}.md"))
    return "".join(parts)
```

```python
"""Command line: python -m ehl_schema.cli build|lint|migrate --workdir <Rowboat data folder>."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .build import build
from .lint import errors, lint
from .migrate import apply, diff, plan
from .model import DEFAULT_SCHEMA, load_schema

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ehl-schema", description="Vault schema: build, lint, migrate")
    ap.add_argument("--schema", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SCHEMA, help="schema file (default: schema/vault-schema.yaml)")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name, text in (("build", "write structure notes, rules note and notes.json"),
                       ("lint", "check every note"), ("migrate", "add missing front matter (dry run by default)")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=text)
        p.add_argument("--workdir", type=Path, required=True, help="Rowboat data folder, e.g. ~/.rowboat-ehl")
    sub.choices["build"].add_argument("--company", default="Company", help="title of the L0 note")
    sub.choices["migrate"].add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write the changes")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    schema = load_schema(args.schema)
    workdir = args.workdir.expanduser()
    vault = workdir / "knowledge"
    if not vault.is_dir():
        log.error("no vault at %s", vault)
        return 2
    if args.command == "build":
        result = build(schema, workdir, args.company)
        log.info("build: %d structure note(s) written, notes.json %s", result["notes"], result["notes_json"])
        return 0
    if args.command == "lint":
        issues = lint(schema, vault)
        for issue in issues:
            log.info("%s %s [%s] %s", issue.severity.upper(), issue.path, issue.code, issue.message)
        n_errors = len(errors(issues))
        log.info("lint: %d error(s), %d warning(s)", n_errors, len(issues) - n_errors)
        return 1 if n_errors else 0
    report = plan(schema, vault)
    if args.write:
        log.info("migrate: wrote %d note(s)", apply(report, vault))
    else:
        if report.changes:
            log.info("%s", diff(report))
        log.info("migrate (dry run): %d note(s) would change; add --write to apply", len(report.changes))
    for path in report.unmapped:
        log.warning("unmapped (folder not in the schema): %s", path)
    for path in report.unresolved:
        log.warning("unresolved (no parent found, no default area): %s", path)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
```
