# Vault folder rules: the VibeMind vault in the schema hierarchy

**Date:** 2026-10-13 · **Status:** draft for review · **Builds on:**
`2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md` (schema) and `2026-10-12-brain-graph-hierarchy-design.md` (graph)

This is **part 1 of 2** of "bring the new Rowboat to VibeMind":

1. **This spec:** the existing VibeMind vault `~/.rowboat/knowledge` is placed into the schema hierarchy,
   and the schema grows the types VibeMind needs. We can see it right away: our fork runs on `~/.rowboat`.
2. **Next spec:** the Rowboat copy in `vibemind-os/spaces/rowboat/rowboat` gets `apps/x` at upstream
   `72e9d8c` + our graph patch, with VibeMind's renderer changes (plugin settings, video link) ported. Its
   web app `apps/rowboat` and `packages/openai-plugin-runtime` stay as they are (upstream deleted
   `apps/rowboat`; there is nothing to merge).

## 1. Goal

Every note of the VibeMind vault gets a type, a level, a domain and a parent, so the 3D brain graph shows
VibeMind as one tree (Company → Domains → Areas → entities → details) and the Rowboat agent can read the
hierarchy. **No existing note is moved, renamed or edited.**

**Success criteria**

- `python -m ehl_schema.cli map --workdir ~/.rowboat --profile vibemind` places every note: each note is
  either in the map with a parent that exists, or excluded on purpose (private). Lint on the VibeMind
  vault has 0 errors.
- Rowboat (our fork) on `~/.rowboat` shows the VibeMind tree in the 3D graph.
- The live writers keep working unchanged: brain curator (`Agents/`, `Hubs/`, `System/`), bubble sync
  (`Bubbles/`, `Projects/`), Marketing (`companys/<Firma>/…`). Their next write does not break the map; the
  next map run picks up new notes.
- The EHL vault behaves exactly as before (same lint result, same graph).

## 2. Findings that shaped this design

From reading `~/.rowboat/knowledge` (503 notes) on 2026-10-13:

| Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `Agents/` (227), `Hubs/`, `System/` were rewritten today, `Bubbles/` two days ago. The writers produce whole files (curator: front matter `typ`, `titel`, nested `fakten`/`belege`; bubble sync: `idea_id`, `sync_version`, …) | **Do not write into existing notes.** Our keys would be overwritten on the next run, and nested YAML must not be touched |
| Marketing reads `companys/<Firma>/Marke.md` and writes `Agent-Notizen/`, `Marke-Verlauf/` by path | **Do not move or rename folders.** The hierarchy hangs on paths |
| Folders do not equal schema types: `companys/`, `vibemind-discourse/`, `Bubbles/`, `Hubs/`, `Videos/`, `Notes/`, `Investor Programs/`, `Coding-Projects/`, `Diary/`, `Bewerbung/` | Mapping needs **path rules**, not just "folder name = type" |
| `Projects/` has three root notes and 38 folders `VibeMind - <Name>/` with `_overview.md`; `VibeMind - E-Ticketing_DE/` holds 97 detail notes; 25 folders are `VibeMind - TODO …` gap items | `_overview` is the project note; other notes in a project folder are its children |
| The graph identifies nodes by `knowledge/<path>.md`; the renderer reads workdir files with `workspace:readFile` (e.g. `config/…`) | A generated `config/vault-map.json` is readable by the graph without a new IPC channel |
| `~/.rowboat/knowledge` is a git repo kept by Rowboat (auto-commits) | New structure notes appear there as normal changes; a backup is still taken before the first write |

## 3. Decisions

- **D1 Path rules, not file edits.** A profile file lists rules "path pattern → type (+ parent)". The
  schema tool resolves them into a map. Existing notes are only read.
- **D2 Front matter wins.** If a note has `type`/`parent`/`level`/`domain` in its own front matter (EHL
  notes), that is used. Rules fill in what is missing.
- **D3 Only new files are written:** structure notes (`Company`, `Domains/*`, `Areas/*`), the rules note
  `Agent Notes/Vault Schema`, and `config/vault-map.json`.
- **D4 One schema, several profiles.** `vault-schema.yaml` stays the single list of domains, areas, types
  and relations. A profile (`schema/profiles/<name>.yaml`) holds what is vault-specific: company name,
  folder rules, excluded paths. The EHL vault uses the built-in default (folder name = type), so nothing
  changes for EHL.
- **D5 Private stays out of the team graph.** `Diary/` and `Bewerbung/` are excluded from the map. Rowboat
  itself still lists them because they sit in the vault; moving them into a private vault is the user's
  later decision and not part of this work.

## 4. Schema changes (`vault-schema.yaml`)

New area:

| Area | Domain |
|---|---|
| Discourse | sources |

New types:

| Type | Domain | Level | Parent (in order) | Default area | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideas | product | 3 | Areas | Roadmap | Idea bubbles (VibeMind `Bubbles/`) |
| Discourse | sources | 4 | Areas | Discourse | Aggregated self-discourse logs |
| Hubs | `*` (from parent) | 3 | Areas | – | Index notes kept by a curator; domain = domain of their parent area |

Widened parent lists (existing EHL notes stay valid; only more parents become allowed):

| Type | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Requirements | Models, Products, Areas | Models, Products, **Projects**, Areas |
| Content | Campaigns, Areas | Campaigns, **Brands**, Areas |
| Agent Notes | Areas | **Brands, Projects, Agents**, Areas |

`model.py` learns the `*` domain for `Hubs` the same way it already handles structure types: lint takes the
expected domain from the parent area.

## 5. Profiles and folder rules

```yaml
# schema/profiles/vibemind.yaml
company: VibeMind
exclude:                     # never in the map, no warning
  - "Diary/**"
  - "Bewerbung/**"
  - "Welcome"                # Rowboat's own welcome note
rules:                       # first match wins; paths are vault-relative, without ".md"
  - {match: "Projects/VibeMind - TODO */_overview", type: Tasks}
  - {match: "Projects/{p}/_overview",               type: Projects}
  - {match: "Projects/{p}/**",                      type: Requirements, parent: "Projects/{p}/_overview"}
  - {match: "Projects/*",                           type: Projects}
  - {match: "Coding-Projects/**",                   type: Projects}
  - {match: "Bubbles/**",                           type: Ideas}
  - {match: "Hubs/Agents",                          type: Hubs, parent: "Areas/Agents"}
  - {match: "Hubs/Bubbles",                         type: Hubs, parent: "Areas/Roadmap"}
  - {match: "Hubs/People",                          type: Hubs, parent: "Areas/Contacts"}
  - {match: "Hubs/System",                          type: Hubs, parent: "Areas/Infrastructure"}
  - {match: "Hubs/*",                               type: Hubs, parent: "Areas/Topics"}
  - {match: "companys/{c}/Marke",                   type: Brands}
  - {match: "companys/{c}/Markenhandbuch",          type: Content, parent: "companys/{c}/Marke"}
  - {match: "companys/{c}/Marke-Verlauf/**",        type: Content, parent: "companys/{c}/Marke"}
  - {match: "companys/{c}/Agent-Notizen/**",        type: Agent Notes, parent: "companys/{c}/Marke"}
  - {match: "vibemind-discourse/**",                type: Discourse}
  - {match: "Videos/**",                            type: Assets}
  - {match: "System/**",                            type: Systems}
  - {match: "Notes/Traction Metrics*",              type: KPIs}
  - {match: "Notes/**",                             type: Topics}
  - {match: "Investor Programs/**",                 type: Funding}
  # everything else: default rule (first folder = type name), e.g. Agents/**, Workflows/**, Topics/**, People/**
```

**Pattern syntax:** `*` matches inside one path segment, `**` matches any number of segments, `{name}`
captures one whole segment and can be used in `parent`. Matching is case-sensitive, like Rowboat links.

**Resolution per note** (in this order):

1. Path in `exclude` → not in the map.
2. Front matter has `type` → use front matter (`parent`, `level`, `domain` from it or from the type).
3. First matching rule → its `type`; `parent` from the rule if given and the target note exists.
4. No rule, but the first folder is a type name → that type (the default rule; this is all the EHL vault
   needs).
5. Nothing fits → type `Topics` under `Areas/Topics`, warning `W-no-rule` with the path.

**Parent when the rule gives none, or its target is missing:** the type's default area
(`Areas/<default_parent>`). A missing rule target also gives warning `W-parent-missing`.

`level` and `domain` come from the type (Hubs: from the parent area). The **profile without a file**
(`--profile` omitted) is the EHL behaviour: company from `--company`, no excludes, only the default rule.

## 6. Generated output

`python -m ehl_schema.cli map --workdir <dir> [--profile <name>] [--company <name>]` reads the vault and
writes **only** these files (each only if its content changed):

- **Structure notes** as today (`Company.md`, `Domains/<Title>.md`, `Areas/<Name>.md`, front matter with
  `managed_by: schema`), including the new area.
- **`Agent Notes/Vault Schema.md`**: the rules note gains a section "Folders in this vault" with the
  profile's rules in plain words, so the agent knows where a new note of a type belongs.
- **`config/vault-map.json`**:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "company": "VibeMind",
  "generated_at": "2026-10-13T14:00:00Z",
  "notes": {
    "Agents/abo-probe (183dc8)": {"type": "Agents", "level": 3, "domain": "ai", "parent": "Areas/Agents"},
    "Areas/Agents": {"type": "Areas", "level": 2, "domain": "ai", "parent": "Domains/AI"}
  }
}
```

Keys and `parent` are vault-relative paths without `.md`. Structure notes are in the map too, so the
graph needs nothing else.

`build` keeps working as today and calls `map` at the end. `install.py` and the vault sync loop run `map`
after every sync, so new notes from the writers appear within one sync interval.

## 7. Graph (fork branch `ehl-schema-graph`)

- `graph-hierarchy.ts` gets `parseVaultMap(json): Map<string, NodeInfo>` (tolerant: wrong version,
  broken JSON or missing fields → empty map) and `buildHierarchyGraph` takes an optional map as fallback:
  per note, front matter values win, the map fills in `level`, `parentId`, `domain`, and a `parent` edge
  for the map's parent.
- `App.tsx` reads `config/vault-map.json` with `workspace:readFile` when building the graph. If the file
  is missing, behaviour is exactly as today.
- The graph reloads the map with the knowledge files (same trigger as today). No new IPC.

## 8. Lint

`lint` takes `--profile` and checks the resolved view (front matter + rules) instead of front matter only:

- Notes placed by a rule are not reported for missing front matter keys.
- New warnings: `W-no-rule` (no rule and first folder is no type), `W-parent-missing` (rule parent does
  not exist).
- All existing checks (cycles, parent level ≤ note level, allowed parent types, relation targets) run on
  the resolved values.
- For the EHL vault (no profile) the result is unchanged.

## 9. Install and start

`scripts/install.py --profile vibemind [--start]`:

- Workdir `~/.rowboat` (overridable with `--workdir`), company from the profile.
- Skips everything BMW/EHL-demo: market venv and data, quotes, Torque app link, `ehl-market` MCP entry, 3D
  car data, demo example data, EHL notes.
- Keeps: tool check, Rowboat clone of our fork, schema install, backup, `build` + `map` + `lint`, start of
  Rowboat in dev mode with `ROWBOAT_WORKDIR=~/.rowboat`, vault-map refresh loop.
- **Backup before the first write:** a copy of `~/.rowboat/knowledge` to
  `~/.rowboat/knowledge.bak-<timestamp>` (once per install run).
- Does not touch `~/.rowboat/config/mcp.json` or other config of the VibeMind installation.

## 10. Error handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Note matches no rule | `Topics` under `Areas/Topics`, warning `W-no-rule` |
| Rule parent missing | Default area of the type, warning `W-parent-missing` |
| Broken front matter or not UTF-8 | Note skipped, reported by lint (as today) |
| Profile file malformed (unknown type, bad pattern, unknown capture in `parent`) | `SchemaError` before anything is written |
| `config/vault-map.json` missing or broken | Graph uses front matter only (today's behaviour) |
| Writer replaces a note while `map` runs | The note is read as it is at that moment; the next run fixes the map |

## 11. Tests

- **pytest** (schema package): pattern matching (`*`, `**`, captures), rule order, excludes, front
  matter precedence, parent fallback + warnings, Hubs domain from parent, map JSON content, "unchanged
  file is not rewritten", profile validation errors, EHL vault result unchanged (existing tests keep
  passing). A fixture vault mirrors the VibeMind folder layout with **made-up** names and content only.
- **vitest** (fork): `parseVaultMap` (good, broken, wrong version), `buildHierarchyGraph` with map
  fallback and front matter precedence.
- **Real run** (not in CI): `map` + `lint` on `~/.rowboat` after the backup; numbers per type and
  warnings reported; Rowboat started on `~/.rowboat`; the user checks the 3D graph.

## 12. Out of scope

- Part 2: updating the Rowboat copy in vibemind-os (own spec).
- Changing the VibeMind writers (curator, bubble sync, Marketing) to write schema front matter.
- Typed relations for VibeMind notes (e.g. a project's `bubble_id` → its idea); only `parent` edges and
  ordinary body links for now.
- Moving `Diary/` and `Bewerbung/` into a private vault.
- Committing anything from `~/.rowboat` to git (real data stays out of the repo).

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\User\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.4.1\skills\writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask

1	"""Vault notes: read a vault, split and extend flat front matter, parse [[links]]."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	import re
6	import unicodedata
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	from datetime import date, datetime
9	from pathlib import Path
10	
11	import yaml
12	
13	LINK = re.compile(r"\[\[([^\]\n]+)\]\]")
14	PLAIN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*")
15	DATE = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")
16	RESERVED = {"true", "false", "yes", "no", "on", "off", "null", "none", "y", "n"}
17	# Rowboat's own memory files: it reads them line by line (inbox) or puts them verbatim into every chat
18	# prompt (user, preferences), so they must never get front matter.
19	ROWBOAT_OWNED = {"Agent Notes/inbox.md", "Agent Notes/user.md", "Agent Notes/preferences.md"}
20	
21	
22	class FrontMatterError(ValueError):
23	    """The front matter is not valid YAML or not a mapping."""
24	
25	
26	@dataclass
27	class Note:
28	    path: str                 # vault-relative, forward slashes, without ".md"
29	    raw: str                  # the file as read (decoded, original newlines)
30	    front: dict | None        # parsed front matter; None if the note has none (or it is broken)
31	    front_text: str           # the lines between the --- fences, "\n"-separated
32	    body: str                 # everything after the closing fence, "\n" newlines
33	    newline: str              # "\r\n" or "\n", as found in the file
34	    error: str | None = None  # why the front matter could not be read
35	
36	
37	def _normalise(value):
38	    if isinstance(value, (date, datetime)):
39	        return value.isoformat()[:10]
40	    if isinstance(value, list):
41	        return [_normalise(v) for v in value]
42	    return value
43	
44	
45	def split(text: str) -> tuple[dict | None, str, str]:
46	    """(front matter or None, raw front matter lines, body). Accepts a BOM and CRLF."""
47	    t = text.lstrip("﻿").replace("\r\n", "\n")
48	    if not t.startswith("---\n"):
49	        return None, "", t
50	    if t.startswith("---\n---\n"):
51	        return {}, "", t[8:]
52	    end = t.find("\n---\n", 3)
53	    if end == -1:
54	        if t.endswith("\n---"):
55	            end = len(t) - 4
56	        else:
57	            return None, "", t
58	    raw = t[4:end]
59	    body = t[end + 5:]
60	    try:
61	        data = yaml.safe_load(raw) or {}
62	    except (yaml.YAMLError, ValueError) as err:  # ValueError: e.g. an impossible date like 2026-02-30
63	        raise FrontMatterError(f"front matter is not valid YAML: {err}") from err
64	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
65	        raise FrontMatterError("front matter is not a mapping")
66	    return {str(k): _normalise(v) for k, v in data.items()}, raw, body
67	
68	
69	def format_value(value) -> str:
70	    """One YAML value as it is written into front matter: plain when safe, JSON-quoted otherwise."""
71	    if isinstance(value, bool):
72	        return "true" if value else "false"
73	    if isinstance(value, int):
74	        return str(value)
75	    if isinstance(value, list):
76	        return json.dumps([str(v) for v in value], ensure_ascii=False)
77	    text = str(value)
78	    if DATE.fullmatch(text) or (PLAIN.fullmatch(text) and text.lower() not in RESERVED):
79	        return text
80	    return json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False)
81	
82	
83	def render_front(fields: dict) -> str:
84	    return "\n".join(f"{key}: {format_value(value)}" for key, value in fields.items())
85	
86	
87	def note_text(fields: dict, body: str) -> str:
88	    return f"---\n{render_front(fields)}\n---\n{body}"
89	
90	
91	def add_keys(note: Note, fields: dict) -> str:
92	    """The note's text with every key of `fields` it does not have yet appended to its front matter.
93	    Existing lines stay first and unchanged; the file's newline style is kept."""
94	    existing = note.front or {}
95	    lines = [line for line in note.front_text.split("\n") if line.strip()] if note.front is not None else []
96	    lines += [f"{key}: {format_value(value)}" for key, value in fields.items() if key not in existing]
97	    text = "---\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n---\n" + note.body
98	    return text.replace("\n", "\r\n") if note.newline == "\r\n" else text
99	
100	
101	def link_target(raw: str) -> str:
102	    return raw.split("|", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0].strip()
103	
104	
105	def links(text: str) -> list[str]:
106	    return [t for t in (link_target(m) for m in LINK.findall(text)) if t]
107	
108	
109	def link_value(value) -> str | None:
110	    """Target of a value that is exactly one [[link]], else None."""
111	    m = LINK.fullmatch(value.strip()) if isinstance(value, str) else None
112	    return link_target(m.group(1)) if m else None
113	
114	
115	def parent_target(note: Note) -> str | None:
116	    return link_value((note.front or {}).get("parent"))
117	
118	
119	def read_vault(vault: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Note], set[str]]:
120	    """All notes (path without .md -> Note) and all file paths. Skips hidden folders such as .git, symlinks
121	    (a write must never leave the vault) and Rowboat's own memory files (ROWBOAT_OWNED)."""
122	    notes: dict[str, Note] = {}
123	    files: set[str] = set()
124	    for file in sorted(vault.rglob("*")):
125	        rel = file.relative_to(vault)
126	        if file.is_symlink() or not file.is_file() or any(part.startswith(".") for part in rel.parts):
127	            continue
128	        key = rel.as_posix()
129	        if key in ROWBOAT_OWNED:
130	            continue
131	        files.add(key)
132	        if file.suffix != ".md":
133	            continue
134	        data = file.read_bytes()
135	        try:
136	            raw = data.decode("utf-8")
137	        except UnicodeDecodeError as err:
138	            raw = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
139	            notes[key[:-3]] = Note(key[:-3], raw, None, "", raw.replace("\r\n", "\n"),
140	                                   "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n", f"not UTF-8: {err}")
141	            continue
142	        newline = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
143	        try:
144	            front, front_text, body = split(raw)
145	            error = None
146	        except FrontMatterError as err:
147	            front, front_text, body, error = None, "", raw.replace("\r\n", "\n"), str(err)
148	        notes[key[:-3]] = Note(key[:-3], raw, front, front_text, body, newline, error)
149	    return notes, files
150	
151	
152	def slug(text: str) -> str:
153	    ascii_text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
154	    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text.lower()).strip("-")

1	"""Check a vault against the schema. Errors break the hierarchy; warnings are worth a look."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import re
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	from pathlib import Path
7	
8	from .model import Schema, TypeDef
9	from .notes import DATE, Note, link_value, links, parent_target, read_vault
10	
11	FIELD = re.compile(r"^\*\*(Email|Domain):\*\*\s*(\S+)", re.M)
12	BASE_KEYS = ("id", "type", "domain", "level")
13	
14	
15	@dataclass(frozen=True)
16	class Issue:
17	    severity: str   # "error" | "warning"
18	    path: str
19	    code: str
20	    message: str
21	
22	
23	def errors(issues: list[Issue]) -> list[Issue]:
24	    return [i for i in issues if i.severity == "error"]

27	def lint(schema: Schema, vault: Path) -> list[Issue]:
28	    notes, files = read_vault(vault)
29	    issues: list[Issue] = []
30	    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
31	    for note in notes.values():
32	        issues.extend(_check_note(schema, note, notes, files, ids))
33	    issues.extend(_check_cycles(notes))
34	    issues.extend(_check_duplicates(notes))

38	def _expected_domain(schema: Schema, tname: str, path: str) -> str | None:
39	    name = path.partition("/")[2]
40	    if tname == "Domains":
41	        return schema.domain_key(name)
42	    if tname == "Areas":
43	        return schema.areas.get(name)

47	def _check_note(schema: Schema, note: Note, notes: dict, files: set, ids: dict) -> list[Issue]:
48	    out: list[Issue] = []
49	
50	    def add(severity: str, code: str, message: str) -> None:
51	        out.append(Issue(severity, note.path, code, message))
52	
53	    tname = schema.type_of_path(note.path)
54	    if tname is None:
55	        add("error", "unknown-type", "the folder of this note is not a note type in the schema")
56	        return out
57	    if note.error:
58	        add("error", "bad-yaml", note.error)
59	        return out
60	    if note.front is None:
61	        add("error", "no-front-matter", "the note has no front matter (run: ehl-schema migrate)")
62	        return out
63	    front = note.front
64	    for key, value in front.items():
65	        if isinstance(value, dict) or (isinstance(value, list) and not all(isinstance(v, str) for v in value)):
66	            add("error", "nested", f"{key!r} must be flat: a value or a list of strings")
67	    needed = BASE_KEYS + (() if tname == "Company" else ("parent",))
68	    for key in needed:
69	        if front.get(key) in (None, ""):
70	            add("error", "missing-key", f"{key!r} is missing")
71	    if out:
72	        return out
73	    td = schema.types[tname]
74	    if front["type"] != tname:
75	        add("error", "type-mismatch", f"type is {front['type']!r}, but the folder says {tname!r}")
76	    if tname != "Company":
77	        expected = _expected_domain(schema, tname, note.path)
78	        if expected is None:
79	            add("error", "not-in-schema", f"{note.path!r} is not a domain or area of the schema")
80	        elif front["domain"] != expected:
81	            add("error", "domain-mismatch", f"domain is {front['domain']!r}, expected {expected!r}")
82	    if front["level"] != td.level:
83	        add("error", "level-mismatch", f"level is {front['level']!r}, expected {td.level}")
84	    first = ids.setdefault(str(front["id"]), note.path)
85	    if first != note.path:
86	        add("error", "duplicate-id", f"id {front['id']!r} is also used by {first!r}")
87	    if tname != "Company":
88	        out.extend(_check_parent(schema, note, td, notes))
89	    out.extend(_check_relations(schema, note, td, notes, files))
90	    if td.statuses and "status" in front and front["status"] not in td.statuses:
91	        add("warning", "status-value", f"status {front['status']!r} is not one of {', '.join(td.statuses)}")
92	    for target in links(note.body):
93	        if target not in notes and target not in files:
94	            add("warning", "broken-link", f"[[{target}]] does not exist")
95	    return out

98	def _check_parent(schema: Schema, note: Note, td: TypeDef, notes: dict) -> list[Issue]:
99	    target = parent_target(note)
100	    if target is None:
101	        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-format", 'parent must be one quoted link like "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"')]
102	    if target not in notes:
103	        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-missing", f"parent [[{target}]] does not exist")]
104	    ptype = schema.type_of_path(target)
105	    if ptype not in td.parent:
106	        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-type",
107	                      f"parent [[{target}]] is a {ptype}; allowed: {', '.join(td.parent)}")]
108	    if schema.types[ptype].level > td.level:
109	        return [Issue("error", note.path, "parent-level", f"parent [[{target}]] is on a lower level than the note")]
110	    return []
111	
112	
113	def _check_relations(schema: Schema, note: Note, td: TypeDef, notes: dict, files: set) -> list[Issue]:
114	    out: list[Issue] = []
115	    front = note.front or {}
116	    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
117	        if name not in front:
118	            if name in td.required:
119	                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "required-relation", f"{name!r} is required"))
120	            continue
121	        value = front[name]
122	        if rel.kind == "date":
123	            if not isinstance(value, str) or not DATE.fullmatch(value):
124	                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-format", f"{name!r} must be a date YYYY-MM-DD"))
125	            continue
126	        targets = [link_value(v) for v in value] if isinstance(value, list) else [None]
127	        if None in targets:
128	            out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-format",
129	                             f'{name!r} must be a list of quoted links like ["[[Folder/Name]]"]'))
130	            continue
131	        if not targets and name in td.required:
132	            out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "required-relation", f"{name!r} must not be empty"))
133	        for target in targets:
134	            if target not in notes and target not in files:
135	                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-missing", f"{name}: [[{target}]] does not exist"))
136	            elif rel.targets is not None and schema.type_of_path(target) not in rel.targets:
137	                out.append(Issue("error", note.path, "relation-target",
138	                                 f"{name}: [[{target}]] must be a {' or '.join(rel.targets)}"))
139	    return out
140	
141	
142	def _check_cycles(notes: dict[str, Note]) -> list[Issue]:
143	    parent = {p: t for p, n in notes.items() if (t := parent_target(n)) is not None}
144	    out, reported = [], set()
145	    for start in parent:
146	        seen, node = [], start
147	        while node in parent and node not in seen:
148	            seen.append(node)
149	            node = parent[node]
150	        if node in seen:
151	            cycle = seen[seen.index(node):]
152	            key = frozenset(cycle)
153	            if key not in reported:
154	                reported.add(key)
155	                out.append(Issue("error", min(cycle), "cycle", "parent chain loops: " + " -> ".join(cycle + [node])))
156	    return out
157	
158	
159	def _check_duplicates(notes: dict[str, Note]) -> list[Issue]:
160	    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
161	    for path, note in notes.items():
162	        folder, _, name = path.partition("/")
163	        if folder not in ("People", "Organizations") or not name:
164	            continue
165	        keys = {("name", folder + ":" + re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", name.lower()))}
166	        for kind, value in FIELD.findall(note.body):
167	            value = value.strip().lower()
168	            if value and not value.startswith("{"):
169	                keys.add((kind.lower(), value))
170	        for key in keys:
171	            groups.setdefault(key, []).append(path)
172	    out = []
173	    for (kind, _), paths in groups.items():
174	        if len(paths) > 1:
175	            for path in paths:
176	                others = ", ".join(p for p in paths if p != path)
177	                out.append(Issue("warning", path, "possible-duplicate", f"same {kind} as {others}"))
178	    return out

1	"""Generate what the schema implies: Company/Domains/Areas notes, the rules note and Rowboat's notes.json."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	import logging
6	from pathlib import Path
7	
8	from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, TypeDef
9	from .notes import note_text, slug, split
10	
11	log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.build")
12	
13	MANAGED = "schema"
14	RULES_NOTE = "Agent Notes/Vault Schema"
15	RULES_MARK = "\n\nSchema rules ("
16	GENERIC_BODY = ("# {Title}\n\n## Summary\n{2-3 sentences.}\n\n## Key facts\n{Substantive facts only. Leave empty if "
17	                "none.}\n\n## Open items\n{Next steps only. Leave empty if none.}\n")

20	def _front(schema: Schema, **fields) -> dict:
21	    # the same keys migrate adds to every note, so build and migrate agree and re-runs settle
22	    return {**fields, "visibility": "team", "env": "prod", "managed_by": MANAGED, "schema_version": schema.version}
23

25	def structure_notes(schema: Schema, company: str) -> dict[str, str]:
26	    notes: dict[str, str] = {}
27	    domain_links = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.domain_note(k)}]]" for k in schema.domains)
28	    notes["Company"] = note_text(
29	        _front(schema, id="company", type="Company", domain="company", level=0),
30	        f"# {company}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Company (L0)\n\n## Domains\n{domain_links}\n")
31	    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
32	        areas = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.area_note(a)}]]" for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
33	        notes[schema.domain_note(key)] = note_text(
34	            _front(schema, id=f"domain-{key}", type="Domains", domain=key, level=1, parent="[[Company]]"),
35	            f"# {title}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Domain (L1)\n**Key:** {key}\n\n## Areas\n{areas}\n")
36	    for area, key in schema.areas.items():
37	        types = ", ".join(n for n, td in schema.types.items() if td.default_parent == area) or "none"
38	        notes[schema.area_note(area)] = note_text(
39	            _front(schema, id=f"area-{slug(area)}", type="Areas", domain=key, level=2,
40	                   parent=f"[[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]"),
41	            f"# {area}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Area (L2)\n**Domain:** [[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]\n"
42	            f"**Note types placed here by default:** {types}\n")
43	    td = schema.types["Agent Notes"]
44	    notes[RULES_NOTE] = note_text(
45	        _front(schema, id="agent-notes-vault-schema", type="Agent Notes", domain=td.domain, level=td.level,
46	               parent=f"[[{schema.area_note(td.default_parent)}]]"),
47	        rules_body(schema))
48	    return notes
49	
50	
51	def rules_body(schema: Schema) -> str:
52	    lines = [f"# Vault schema (v{schema.version})", "",
53	             "Generated from schema/vault-schema.yaml by `ehl-schema build`. Do not edit; change the schema file.", "",
54	             "## Front matter", "",
55	             "Every note starts with flat YAML front matter. Required keys: id, type, domain, level, parent.",
56	             "- `id`: a stable slug; never change it. `type`: the folder name. `level`: from the table below.",
57	             '- `parent`: exactly one quoted link, for example `parent: "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"`.',
58	             '- Relations are lists of quoted links with the full path, for example `about: ["[[Areas/Pipeline]]"]`.',
59	             "- Never nest keys. Optional: status, visibility (team | restricted), env (prod | test), when (YYYY-MM-DD).",
60	             "", "## Domains and areas", "", "| Domain | Key | Areas |", "|---|---|---|"]
61	    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
62	        areas = ", ".join(a for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
63	        lines.append(f"| {title} | {key} | {areas} |")
64	    lines += ["", "## Note types", "",
65	              "| Type (folder) | Domain | Level | Parent (in order) | Default area | Required | Optional |",
66	              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
67	    for name, td in schema.types.items():
68	        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
69	            continue
70	        lines.append(f"| {name} | {td.domain} | {td.level} | {', '.join(td.parent)} | {td.default_parent or ''} | "
71	                     f"{', '.join(td.required) or '–'} | {', '.join(td.optional) or '–'} |")
72	    lines += ["", "## Relations", "", "| Key | Points to |", "|---|---|"]
73	    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
74	        target = "a date" if rel.kind == "date" else ("any note" if rel.targets is None else ", ".join(rel.targets))
75	        lines.append(f"| {name} | {target} |")
76	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
77	
78	
79	def write_structure(schema: Schema, vault: Path, company: str) -> int:
80	    written = 0
81	    for path, text in structure_notes(schema, company).items():
82	        file = vault / f"{path}.md"
83	        if file.exists():
84	            old = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
85	            if old == text:
86	                continue
87	            front, _, _ = split(old)
88	            if (front or {}).get("managed_by") != MANAGED:
89	                log.warning("%s exists and is not managed by the schema; left as it is", file)
90	                continue
91	        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
92	        file.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
93	        written += 1
94	    return written

97	def _parent_hint(td: TypeDef) -> str:
98	    if td.parent == ("Areas",):
99	        return f"Areas/{td.default_parent}"
100	    options = ", ".join(f"{p}/…" for p in td.parent if p != "Areas")

104	def _skeleton(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
105	    lines = ["---", "id: {slug of the title}", f"type: {td.name}", f"domain: {td.domain}", f"level: {td.level}",
106	             f'parent: "[[{{{_parent_hint(td)}}}]]"']

118	def _guide(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
119	    default = f" (else [[Areas/{td.default_parent}]])" if td.default_parent else ""
120	    return (f"v{schema.version}): flat YAML front matter. type: {td.name}; domain: {td.domain}; level: {td.level}; "
121	            f"id: a stable slug, never change it. parent: exactly one quoted link to a note of type "
122	            f"{', '.join(td.parent)}{default}. Required relations: {', '.join(td.required) or 'none'}. "
123	            f"Optional relations: {', '.join(td.optional) or 'none'}. Relation values are lists of quoted "
124	            f'full-path links like ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]. Status: {", ".join(td.statuses) or "free text"}.')
125	
126	
127	def _strip_front(template: str) -> str:
128	    """The template body without a leading --- block. Text-based: template placeholders are not always YAML."""
129	    t = template.replace("\r\n", "\n")
130	    if t.startswith("---\n"):
131	        end = t.find("\n---\n", 3)
132	        if end != -1:
133	            return t[end + 5:]
134	    return t
135	
136	
137	def notes_json(schema: Schema, existing: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
138	    by_type = {e["type"]: dict(e) for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e}
139	    order = [e["type"] for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e]
140	    for name, td in schema.types.items():
141	        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES or (td.builtin and name not in by_type):
142	            continue
143	        entry = by_type.get(name, {"type": name, "folder": name, "template": "", "extractionGuide": ""})
144	        if name not in by_type:
145	            order.append(name)
146	        template = entry.get("template") or ""
147	        if not (td.builtin and not template.strip()):
148	            body = _strip_front(template)
149	            body = body if body.strip() else (td.template or GENERIC_BODY)
150	            entry["template"] = _skeleton(schema, td) + body
151	        guide = (entry.get("extractionGuide") or "").split(RULES_MARK)[0]
152	        entry["extractionGuide"] = guide + RULES_MARK + _guide(schema, td)
153	        by_type[name] = entry
154	    return [by_type[name] for name in order]
155	
156	
157	def build(schema: Schema, workdir: Path, company: str) -> dict:
158	    written = write_structure(schema, workdir / "knowledge", company)
159	    config = workdir / "config" / "notes.json"
160	    if not config.exists():
161	        log.warning("%s does not exist yet: start Rowboat once, then run build again", config)
162	        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "missing"}
163	    old = config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
164	    new = json.dumps(notes_json(schema, json.loads(old)), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
165	    if new == old:
166	        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "unchanged"}
167	    config.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
168	    return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "updated"}

17	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
18	    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
19	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="ehl-schema", description="Vault schema: build, lint, migrate")
20	    ap.add_argument("--schema", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SCHEMA, help="schema file (default: schema/vault-schema.yaml)")
21	    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
22	    for name, text in (("build", "write structure notes, rules note and notes.json"),
23	                       ("lint", "check every note"), ("migrate", "add missing front matter (dry run by default)")):
24	        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=text)
25	        p.add_argument("--workdir", type=Path, required=True, help="Rowboat data folder, e.g. ~/.rowboat-ehl")
26	    sub.choices["build"].add_argument("--company", default="Company", help="title of the L0 note")
27	    sub.choices["migrate"].add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write the changes")
28	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
29	
30	    schema = load_schema(args.schema)
31	    workdir = args.workdir.expanduser()
32	    vault = workdir / "knowledge"
33	    if not vault.is_dir():
34	        log.error("no vault at %s", vault)
35	        return 2
36	    if args.command == "build":
37	        result = build(schema, workdir, args.company)
38	        log.info("build: %d structure note(s) written, notes.json %s", result["notes"], result["notes_json"])
39	        return 0
40	    if args.command == "lint":
41	        issues = lint(schema, vault)
42	        for issue in issues:
43	            log.info("%s %s [%s] %s", issue.severity.upper(), issue.path, issue.code, issue.message)
44	        n_errors = len(errors(issues))
45	        log.info("lint: %d error(s), %d warning(s)", n_errors, len(issues) - n_errors)
46	        return 1 if n_errors else 0
47	    report = plan(schema, vault)
48	    if args.write:
49	        log.info("migrate: wrote %d note(s)", apply(report, vault))
50	    else:
51	        if report.changes:
52	            log.info("%s", diff(report))
53	        log.info("migrate (dry run): %d note(s) would change; add --write to apply", len(report.changes))
54	    for path in report.unmapped:
55	        log.warning("unmapped (folder not in the schema): %s", path)
56	    for path in report.unresolved:
57	        log.warning("unresolved (no parent found, no default area): %s", path)
58	    return 0
59	
60

62	    sys.exit(main())

"""Helpers for the schema tests: write notes and small valid vaults."""
from pathlib import Path

from ehl_schema.notes import note_text


def write_note(vault: Path, path: str, front: dict | None, body: str = "") -> Path:
    file = vault / f"{path}.md"
    file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    file.write_text(note_text(front, body) if front is not None else body, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return file


def structure(schema, key: str, area: str) -> dict:
    """front matter of the domain note and the area note a test needs."""
    return {
        schema.domain_note(key): {"id": f"domain-{key}", "type": "Domains", "domain": key, "level": 1,
                                  "parent": "[[Company]]"},
        schema.area_note(area): {"id": f"area-{area.lower()}", "type": "Areas", "domain": key, "level": 2,
                                 "parent": f"[[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]"},
    }


def valid_vault(tmp_path: Path, schema) -> Path:
    vault = tmp_path / "knowledge"

# Vault Folder Rules Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Place every note of the VibeMind vault (`~/.rowboat/knowledge`) into the schema hierarchy through
path rules, without editing any existing note, and show the result in our fork's 3D brain graph.

**Architecture:** A profile file (`schema/profiles/vibemind.yaml`) holds company name, excludes and path
rules. A new resolver turns notes + profile into a placement per note (type, level, domain, parent). A new
`map` command writes structure notes plus `config/vault-map.json`. Lint checks the resolved view. The Rowboat
renderer reads the map as a fallback for notes without hierarchy front matter. The installer gets a
`--profile vibemind` path without any BMW/EHL demo step.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12 + PyYAML + pytest (`schema/`), stdlib-only installer (`scripts/install.py`),
TypeScript + React + vitest in the Rowboat fork (`C:\Users\User\Desktop\rowboat`, branch `ehl-schema-graph`).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-vault-folder-rules-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Python 3.12, `logging` (no `print`), runs on Windows and macOS; every text write uses `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
- `scripts/install.py` uses the standard library only (it runs before anything is installed).
- No existing vault note is moved, renamed or edited; only `Company.md`, `Domains/*`, `Areas/*`,
  `Agent Notes/Vault Schema.md` and `config/vault-map.json` are written.
- `migrate` must never run on a profile vault.
- The EHL vault without `--profile` behaves exactly as before (all existing tests keep passing, same lint result).
- Real data stays out of git: nothing from `~/.rowboat*` is committed; test fixtures use made-up names only.
- Commits: conventional commits, prefix the command with `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` (the Entire hook hangs otherwise),
  end the message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- EHL repo branch: `feat/vault-folder-rules`. Rowboat fork branch: `ehl-schema-graph` (local, not pushed yet).
- Spec warning names map to lint codes: `W-no-rule` → warning `no-rule`, `W-parent-missing` → warning `rule-parent-missing`.
- Run schema tests with: `cd schema && py -3.12 -m pytest -q` (Windows) / `python3.12 -m pytest -q` (macOS).
- Run renderer tests with: `cd C:\Users\User\Desktop\rowboat\apps\x\apps\renderer && npx vitest run src/lib/graph-hierarchy.test.ts`, typecheck `npx tsc -b`.

## Review Focus

1. **The installer's VibeMind path runs `migrate`** → it would write front matter into 500 live notes. Expect: the
   profile command list contains no `migrate` (test in Task 7).
2. **`vault-map.json` rewritten on every run although nothing changed** (only `generated_at` differs) → Rowboat's
   knowledge git and the graph churn every minute. Expect: an unchanged map is not rewritten (test in Task 4).
3. **Real VibeMind file names** with spaces, parentheses, em dashes, umlauts and dots (`LinkedIn Launch — Agentic OS
   Beta opens (c1c67f)`, `Traction Metrics 2026-Q2`) → regex special characters must be escaped. Expect: they match
   their rule (test in Task 2).
4. **Curator front matter** (`typ:`, nested `fakten:` lists, a foreign `type: coding-project`) → must neither win
   placement nor produce lint errors. Expect: the rule places the note, lint is clean (tests in Tasks 3 and 5).
5. **Company name drift**: the EHL refresh loop calling `map` without `--company EHL` would rewrite `Company.md`
   to "Company". Expect: every installer `map` command carries the company (test in Task 7).

---

## File Structure

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `schema/vault-schema.yaml` (modify) | New area Discourse, types Ideas/Discourse/Hubs, widened parent lists |
| `schema/ehl_schema/model.py` (modify) | Accept domain `*` for index types (Hubs) |
| `schema/ehl_schema/issues.py` (create) | `Issue` dataclass shared by lint and resolver |
| `schema/ehl_schema/profile.py` (create) | Profile file loading, path pattern compiling and matching |
| `schema/ehl_schema/placement.py` (create) | Resolve every note to a `Placement` (front matter, rule, default, fallback) |
| `schema/ehl_schema/vaultmap.py` (create) | Build/write `config/vault-map.json`, run the whole `map` step |
| `schema/ehl_schema/build.py` (modify) | Rules note gains "Folders in this vault"; skip `*` types in notes.json |
| `schema/ehl_schema/lint.py` (modify) | Profile mode: check the resolved view |
| `schema/ehl_schema/migrate.py` (modify) | Leave `*` types (Hubs) alone |
| `schema/ehl_schema/cli.py` (modify) | `map` command, `--profile` on build/lint/map, `--watch` |
| `schema/profiles/vibemind.yaml` (create) | The VibeMind rules from spec §5 |
| `schema/tests/helpers.py` (modify) | `vibemind_like_vault()` fixture with made-up content |
| `schema/tests/test_profile.py`, `test_placement.py`, `test_vaultmap.py` (create) | Tests |
| `scripts/install.py` (modify) | `--profile`, backup, schema venv, map refresh job |
| `scripts/tests/test_install.py` (modify) | Tests for the new pure helpers |

```python
"""Vault profiles: company name, excluded paths and folder rules (path pattern -> note type).

Pattern syntax (paths are vault-relative, without ".md"): `*` matches inside one segment, `**` matches one or
more whole segments, `{name}` captures one whole segment for use in a rule's `parent`. Case-sensitive.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

from .model import DEFAULT_SCHEMA, STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, SchemaError

PROFILES_DIR = DEFAULT_SCHEMA.parent / "profiles"
CAPTURE = re.compile(r"\{(\w+)\}")


def compile_pattern(pattern: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    parts = []
    for part in pattern.split("/"):
        whole = CAPTURE.fullmatch(part)
        if part == "**":
            parts.append(r"[^/]+(?:/[^/]+)*")
        elif whole:
            parts.append(f"(?P<{whole.group(1)}>[^/]+)")
        elif "{" in part or "}" in part or "**" in part or not part:
            raise SchemaError(f"bad path pattern {pattern!r}: {part!r}")
        else:
            parts.append("[^/]*".join(re.escape(s) for s in part.split("*")))
    try:
        return re.compile("/".join(parts))
    except re.error as err:  # e.g. the same capture twice
        raise SchemaError(f"bad path pattern {pattern!r}: {err}") from err


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rule:
    match: str
    type: str
    parent: str | None
    regex: re.Pattern[str]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Profile:
    company: str
    rules: tuple[Rule, ...] = ()
    exclude: tuple[re.Pattern[str], ...] = ()
    name: str = "default"

    @property
    def has_rules(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.rules or self.exclude)

    def excludes(self, path: str) -> bool:
        return any(p.fullmatch(path) for p in self.exclude)

    def match(self, path: str) -> tuple[Rule, dict[str, str]] | None:
        for rule in self.rules:
            m = rule.regex.fullmatch(path)
            if m:
                return rule, m.groupdict()
        return None


def default_profile(company: str) -> Profile:
    """Every note lives in the folder of its type (the EHL vault)."""
    return Profile(company)


def _rule(raw: object, schema: Schema) -> Rule:
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not isinstance(raw.get("match"), str) or not isinstance(raw.get("type"), str):
        raise SchemaError(f"rule {raw!r}: needs 'match' and 'type'")
    tname, parent = raw["type"], raw.get("parent")
    if tname not in schema.types or tname in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
        raise SchemaError(f"rule {raw['match']!r}: {tname!r} is not a note type of the schema")
    regex = compile_pattern(raw["match"])
    if parent is not None:
        if not isinstance(parent, str):
            raise SchemaError(f"rule {raw['match']!r}: parent must be a path")
        unknown = set(CAPTURE.findall(parent)) - set(regex.groupindex)
        if unknown:
            raise SchemaError(f"rule {raw['match']!r}: parent uses {sorted(unknown)} not captured in match")
    return Rule(raw["match"], tname, parent, regex)


def load_profile(ref: str, schema: Schema) -> Profile:
    path = Path(ref) if ref.endswith((".yaml", ".yml")) else PROFILES_DIR / f"{ref}.yaml"
    if not path.is_file():
        raise SchemaError(f"no profile {ref!r} (looked for {path})")
    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not isinstance(raw.get("company"), str) or not raw["company"].strip():
        raise SchemaError(f"{path}: a profile needs 'company'")
    rules = tuple(_rule(r, schema) for r in raw.get("rules") or [])
    exclude = tuple(compile_pattern(str(p)) for p in raw.get("exclude") or [])
    return Profile(raw["company"].strip(), rules, exclude, path.stem)
```

```python
"""Where every note sits in the hierarchy: from its own front matter, a profile rule, the default rule
(first folder = type) or the fallback (Topics). Reads notes only; never writes."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .issues import Issue
from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema
from .notes import Note, parent_target
from .profile import Profile

FALLBACK_TYPE = "Topics"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Placement:
    type: str
    level: int
    domain: str
    parent: str | None   # vault-relative path without ".md"; None only for the Company note
    source: str          # "front" | "rule" | "default" | "fallback"


@dataclass
class Resolution:
    placements: dict[str, Placement] = field(default_factory=dict)
    excluded: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    issues: list[Issue] = field(default_factory=list)


def _from_front(schema: Schema, note: Note) -> Placement | None:
    front = note.front or {}
    tname = front.get("type")
    if not isinstance(tname, str) or tname not in schema.types:
        return None
    td = schema.types[tname]
    level = front.get("level") if isinstance(front.get("level"), int) else td.level
    domain = str(front.get("domain") or td.domain)
    return Placement(tname, level, domain, parent_target(note), "front")


def _area_domain(schema: Schema, parent: str) -> str:
    folder, _, name = parent.partition("/")
    return schema.areas.get(name, "knowledge") if folder == "Areas" else "knowledge"


def resolve(schema: Schema, profile: Profile, notes: dict[str, Note]) -> Resolution:
    res = Resolution()
    pending: dict[str, tuple[str, str | None, str]] = {}
    for path in sorted(notes):
        if profile.excludes(path):
            res.excluded.append(path)
            continue
        placed = _from_front(schema, notes[path])
        if placed is not None:
            res.placements[path] = placed
            continue
        hit = profile.match(path)
        folder, sep, _ = path.partition("/")
        if hit is not None:
            rule, captures = hit
            parent = rule.parent.format_map(captures) if rule.parent else None
            pending[path] = (rule.type, parent, "rule")
        elif sep and folder in schema.types and folder not in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
            pending[path] = (folder, None, "default")
        else:
            pending[path] = (FALLBACK_TYPE, None, "fallback")
            res.issues.append(Issue("warning", path, "no-rule",
                                    f"no folder rule for this path; placed under Areas/{FALLBACK_TYPE}"))
    for path, (tname, parent, source) in pending.items():
        td = schema.types[tname]
        if parent is not None and (parent not in notes or profile.excludes(parent)):
            res.issues.append(Issue("warning", path, "rule-parent-missing",
                                    f"rule parent [[{parent}]] does not exist; placed under its default area"))
            parent = None
        if parent is None:
            parent = schema.area_note(td.default_parent or FALLBACK_TYPE)
        domain = _area_domain(schema, parent) if td.domain == "*" else td.domain
        res.placements[path] = Placement(tname, td.level, domain, parent, source)
    return res
```

```python
"""config/vault-map.json: the resolved hierarchy of every note, read by Rowboat's brain graph as a fallback for
notes without hierarchy front matter. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-vault-folder-rules-design.md §6."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from .build import write_structure
from .issues import Issue
from .model import Schema
from .notes import read_vault
from .placement import Resolution, resolve
from .profile import Profile

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.vaultmap")

MAP_FILE = Path("config") / "vault-map.json"
MAP_VERSION = 1


@dataclass
class MapResult:
    structure: int
    notes: int
    excluded: int
    issues: list[Issue]
    written: bool


def map_document(company: str, res: Resolution) -> dict:
    notes = {path: {"type": p.type, "level": p.level, "domain": p.domain, "parent": p.parent}
             for path, p in sorted(res.placements.items())}
    return {"version": MAP_VERSION, "company": company,
            "generated_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), "notes": notes}


def _same(old_text: str, doc: dict) -> bool:
    try:
        old = json.loads(old_text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return False
    if not isinstance(old, dict):
        return False
    return {k: v for k, v in old.items() if k != "generated_at"} == {k: v for k, v in doc.items() if k != "generated_at"}


def write_map(workdir: Path, doc: dict) -> bool:
    file = workdir / MAP_FILE
    if file.exists() and _same(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), doc):
        return False
    file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    file.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return True


def run_map(schema: Schema, profile: Profile, workdir: Path) -> MapResult:
    vault = workdir / "knowledge"
    structure = write_structure(schema, vault, profile.company, profile)
    notes, _ = read_vault(vault)
    res = resolve(schema, profile, notes)
    written = write_map(workdir, map_document(profile.company, res))
    return MapResult(structure, len(res.placements), len(res.excluded), res.issues, written)
```

```python
def _cycles(parent: dict[str, str]) -> list[Issue]:
    out, reported = [], set()
    for start in parent:
        seen, node = [], start
        while node in parent and node not in seen:
            seen.append(node)
            node = parent[node]
        if node in seen:
            cycle = seen[seen.index(node):]
            key = frozenset(cycle)
            if key not in reported:
                reported.add(key)
                out.append(Issue("error", min(cycle), "cycle", "parent chain loops: " + " -> ".join(cycle + [node])))
    return out
```

```ts
const VAULT_MAP_VERSION = 1

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
}

/** config/vault-map.json (written by `ehl-schema map`): node id -> hierarchy info. Any problem gives an empty map,
 * so the graph falls back to front matter only. */
export function parseVaultMap(text: string, toNodeId: (wikiPath: string) => string | null): Map<string, NodeInfo> {
  const out = new Map<string, NodeInfo>()
  let doc: unknown
  try {
    doc = JSON.parse(text)
  } catch {
    return out
  }
  if (!isRecord(doc) || doc.version !== VAULT_MAP_VERSION || !isRecord(doc.notes)) return out
  for (const [path, entry] of Object.entries(doc.notes)) {
    if (!isRecord(entry) || !Number.isInteger(entry.level)) continue
    const id = toNodeId(path)
    if (!id) continue
    const parentId = typeof entry.parent === 'string' ? toNodeId(entry.parent) ?? undefined : undefined
    out.set(id, {
      level: entry.level as number,
      domain: typeof entry.domain === 'string' ? entry.domain : undefined,
      parentId,
    })
  }
  return out
}
```

```ts
/** Typed edges (one per unordered pair, strongest kind wins) and hierarchy info per node. Front matter wins;
 * `fallback` (from the vault map) fills in level, domain and parent for notes that have none. */
export function buildHierarchyGraph(
  contents: { path: string; data: string }[],
  nodeSet: Set<string>,
  toNodeId: (wikiTarget: string) => string | null,
  fallback?: Map<string, NodeInfo>,
): { edges: HierarchyEdge[]; info: Map<string, NodeInfo> } {
  const edges = new Map<string, HierarchyEdge>()
  const info = new Map<string, NodeInfo>()
  const addEdge = (source: string, target: string, kind: EdgeKind, relation?: string) => {
    if (target === source || !nodeSet.has(target)) return
    const key = source < target ? `${source}|${target}` : `${target}|${source}`
    const existing = edges.get(key)
    if (existing && RANK[existing.kind] >= RANK[kind]) return
    edges.set(key, relation ? { source, target, kind, relation } : { source, target, kind })
  }
  const add = (source: string, rawTarget: string, kind: EdgeKind, relation?: string) => {
    const target = toNodeId(rawTarget)
    if (target) addEdge(source, target, kind, relation)
  }
  for (const { path, data } of contents) {
    const hierarchy = parseHierarchy(data)
    const mapped = fallback?.get(path)
    const frontParent = hierarchy.parent ? toNodeId(hierarchy.parent) : null
    const mappedParent = !hierarchy.parent && mapped?.parentId && nodeSet.has(mapped.parentId) ? mapped.parentId : undefined
    info.set(path, {
      level: hierarchy.level ?? mapped?.level,
      parentId: frontParent && nodeSet.has(frontParent) ? frontParent : mappedParent,
      domain: hierarchy.domain ?? mapped?.domain,
    })
    if (hierarchy.parent) add(path, hierarchy.parent, 'parent')
    else if (mappedParent) addEdge(path, mappedParent, 'parent')
    for (const relation of hierarchy.relations) add(path, relation.target, 'relation', relation.name)
    for (const match of data.matchAll(LINK)) add(path, match[1], 'link')
  }
  return { edges: Array.from(edges.values()), info }
}
```

```python
def profile_company(name: str) -> str:
    """The company name of a vault profile (schema/profiles/<name>.yaml); stdlib only, so no YAML parser."""
    path = PROFILES / f"{name}.yaml"
    if not path.is_file():
        raise InstallError(f"no profile {name!r} in {PROFILES}")
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep and key.strip() == "company" and value.split("#")[0].strip():
            return value.split("#")[0].strip().strip("'\"")
    raise InstallError(f"{path} has no company")


def _schema_cli(py: Path) -> list[str]:
    return [str(py), "-m", "ehl_schema.cli"]


def schema_commands(py: Path, workdir: Path, company: str, profile: str | None) -> list[list[str]]:
    """build (+ migrate for the EHL vault only) + map. A profile vault is never migrated: its notes belong to
    live writers and must not be edited."""
    w = ["--workdir", str(workdir)]
    prof = ["--profile", profile] if profile else []
    cmds = [_schema_cli(py) + ["build", *w, "--company", company, *prof]]
    if profile is None:
        cmds.append(_schema_cli(py) + ["migrate", *w, "--write"])
    cmds.append(_schema_cli(py) + ["map", *w, "--company", company, *prof])
    return cmds


def map_watch_command(py: Path, workdir: Path, company: str, profile: str | None,
                      seconds: int = MAP_REFRESH_SECONDS) -> list[str]:
    prof = ["--profile", profile] if profile else []
    return _schema_cli(py) + ["map", "--workdir", str(workdir), "--company", company, *prof, "--watch", str(seconds)]


def backup_vault(vault: Path, stamp: str) -> Path | None:
    """Copy the vault next to itself (knowledge.bak-<stamp>), without its .git folder."""
    if not vault.is_dir():
        return None
    dest = vault.with_name(f"{vault.name}.bak-{stamp}")
    shutil.copytree(vault, dest, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(".git"), dirs_exist_ok=True)
    return dest
```

```python
def start(rowboat: Path, workdir: Path, company: str = "EHL", profile: str | None = None) -> int:
    """Start Rowboat and its helpers; Ctrl+C stops all of them. With a profile only Rowboat and the
    vault-map refresh run (no BMW demo syncs, no RAG)."""
    vault = str(workdir / "knowledge")
    env = {**os.environ, "ROWBOAT_WORKDIR": str(workdir), "EHL_VAULT": vault}
    jobs = [("Rowboat", ["npm", "run", "dev"], rowboat / "apps" / "x")]
    if profile:
        schema_py = venv_python(ROOT / "schema" / ".venv")
        jobs.append(("vault map", map_watch_command(schema_py, workdir, company, profile), ROOT))
    else:
        market_py, search_py = venv_python(ROOT / "market" / ".venv"), venv_python(ROOT / "search" / ".venv")
        jobs += [("vault sync", [str(market_py), str(ROOT / "demo" / "visu" / "vault.py"), "sync", "--watch",
                                 "--vault", vault], ROOT),
                 ("Torque sync", [str(market_py), str(ROOT / "demo" / "torque" / "sync.py"), "--watch",
                                  "--vault", vault], ROOT),
                 ("vault map", map_watch_command(market_py, workdir, company, None), ROOT)]
        if search_py.exists():
            jobs.append(("RAG", [str(search_py), "-m", "uvicorn", "app:app", "--port", str(RAG_PORT)], ROOT))
    procs = []
    for name, cmd, cwd in jobs:
        log.info("starting %s: %s", name, " ".join(cmd))
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=env, shell=IS_WINDOWS and cmd[0] == "npm"))
    log.info("Rowboat opens after its first build (a few minutes). Ctrl+C stops everything.")
    try:
        procs[0].wait()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        for proc in procs:
            stop(proc)
    return 0
```

Der Plan ist fertig und gepusht: [docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-vault-folder-rules-plan.md](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-13-vault-folder-rules-plan.md) (Commit `faf1af0`).

**8 Tasks:**
1. **Schema erweitern:** neue Typen Ideas, Discourse und Hubs, neuer Bereich Discourse, drei Typen bekommen zusätzliche Elternknoten. `migrate` lässt Hubs in Ruhe.
2. **Profile und Pfadmuster:** `profile.py` plus `schema/profiles/vibemind.yaml`.
3. **Einordnung jeder Notiz:** nach Front-Matter, Regel, Standardregel oder Rückfall. Getestet wird mit einer nachgebauten Vibemind-Struktur mit erfundenen Namen.
4. **Neuer Befehl `map`:** schreibt die Struktur-Notizen, einen neuen Abschnitt in der Regel-Notiz und `config/vault-map.json`. Ist die Map unverändert, wird sie nicht neu geschrieben.

6. **3D-Graph im Fork:** liest `vault-map.json` als Rückfall. Hat eine Notiz eigene Hierarchie-Felder in der Front-Matter, haben die Vorrang.

8. **Echter Lauf auf `~/.rowboat`:** prüfen, dass keine bestehende Notiz geändert wurde, dann Rowboat starten und du schaust dir den 3D-Graphen an. Dazu kommt die Doku.

**Darauf achtet die Prüfung besonders (je mit eigenem Test):**

# Executing Plans

Execute the plan yourself, task by task, in this session: no implementer
subagent per task, no reviewer per task. One fresh-context review of the
whole branch at the end.

**Why inline:** Subagent-driven development pays for a fresh implementer
and a fresh reviewer on every task, each re-reading the codebase from zero.
Inline execution pays for one context (yours) plus one reviewer at the end.
What it gives up is a fresh context per task and a second pair of eyes per
task. This skill keeps what those two things bought, by other means: the
brief is the spec, the ledger is your memory, TDD is the per-task gate, and
the final reviewer is the second pair of eyes.

**Core principle:** The plan already did the thinking. Execute it exactly,
prove each step with a test you watched fail and then pass, and leave a
record that survives your own forgetting.

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner
between tasks. They chose inline execution to spend less, not to answer
"should I continue?" after every task. Execute all tasks from the plan
without stopping.

**Rulings, not stalls.** Conflicts, ambiguities, plan defects — decide them.
The spec is the binding authority, the plan is its argument, and your
judgment settles what neither answers. Record every decision in the ledger
as `Ruling: <what you decided> — <why> — <what it costs if wrong>`, and keep
going. Deviating from the plan without a ledgered ruling is a decision made
in secret.

Four things stop you, and only these: an irreversible or destructive
operation; a security-sensitive action; a side effect outside this worktree
that norms say you ask about first (a merge, a push to a shared branch, a
publish); and a plan so broken that every path forward is a guess. For
those, stop and ask.

## When to Use

- You have a plan from superpowers:writing-plans and your human partner
  chose inline execution at the handoff.
- Your harness has no subagent tool (see the per-platform references in
  `../using-superpowers/references/`). Never fabricate a dispatch; run
  the plan here.
- Tasks are mostly independent — the same precondition as
  superpowers:subagent-driven-development.

A fully specified plan makes inline execution transcription plus testing:
it runs well on a mid-tier session model, and the one place the most
capable model earns its cost is the final review, which this skill
dispatches separately. Tell your human partner so when they choose inline.

Prefer superpowers:subagent-driven-development when your human partner
wants a review gate on every task, or when the plan is long enough that
its later tasks would run on a compacted context. Inline execution over a
long plan still works — the ledger is what makes it recoverable — but the
last tasks get the least of you.
